# The Elder Millennial Chronicles

> Old fables, fairy tales and myths from around the world, told the old way: the moral first, the consequences intact. Illustrated read-aloud books for ages 6 to 12 by Michael A. Mancuso with Gigi and Enzo Mancuso, published by Mancuso Family Press, LLC.

- [All the books](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/books/)
- [For parents](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/parents/)
- [About and press kit](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/about/)

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: The Tales Everyone Knows

- [The Boy Who Cried Wolf](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-boy-who-cried-wolf/): Lie often enough, and nobody comes when it’s true.
- [The Tortoise and the Hare](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-tortoise-and-the-hare/): Slow and steady wins. Fast and lazy loses, in public.
- [The Ant and the Grasshopper](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-ant-and-the-grasshopper/): Summer ends. It always ends.
- [The Fox and the Crow](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-fox-and-the-crow/): When someone flatters you, check what you are holding.
- [The Three Little Pigs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-three-little-pigs/): Do the hard work now, or the wolf will do it for you.
- [The Little Red Hen](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-little-red-hen/): No work, no bread. Not even a crumb.
- [The Goose That Laid the Golden Eggs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-goose-that-laid-the-golden-eggs/): Greed kills the thing that feeds you.
- [The Milkmaid and Her Pail](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-milkmaid-and-her-pail/): Count your chickens, and you may spill the milk.
- [Henny Penny](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/henny-penny/): Panic makes you very easy to catch.
- [The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-town-mouse-and-the-country-mouse/): Better a crust in peace than a feast with the cat.
- [The Wolf in Sheep’s Clothing](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-wolf-in-sheeps-clothing/): A disguise doesn’t change what you are.
- [The Frogs Who Wanted a King](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-frogs-who-wanted-a-king/): Be careful what you beg for.
- [The Scorpion and the Frog](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-scorpion-and-the-frog/): When someone shows you who they are, believe them.
- [Little Red Riding Hood](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/little-red-riding-hood/): Never tell a stranger where you are going.
- [Hansel and Gretel](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/hansel-and-gretel/): Free sweets always come with a bill.
- [The Frog Prince](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-frog-prince/): A promise made to a frog is still a promise.
- [Jack and the Beanstalk](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/jack-and-the-beanstalk/): Steal from a giant, and the giant follows you home.
- [The Ugly Duckling](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-ugly-duckling/): The farmyard doesn’t decide what you are. Get through the winter.
- [The Three Billy Goats Gruff](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-three-billy-goats-gruff/): Bullies keep collecting until someone bigger shows up.
- [Mother Holle](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/mother-holle/): Shirk the work, and you will wear the wages.
- [The Wolf and the Seven Young Goats](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-wolf-and-the-seven-young-goats/): Know who is at the door before you open it.
- [Rumpelstiltskin](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/rumpelstiltskin/): Never promise later what you would not give today.
- [The Fisherman and His Wife](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-fisherman-and-his-wife/): Never satisfied is the shortest road to nothing.
- [Goldilocks and the Three Bears](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/goldilocks-and-the-three-bears/): Don’t take what isn’t yours.
- [Diamonds and Toads](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/diamonds-and-toads/): Mind your manners. Your mouth will tell on you.
- [Cinderella (The Original)](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/cinderella-the-original/): Cheaters get caught, and cheating costs them.
- [The Goose Girl](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-goose-girl/): Be careful what punishment you name. It may be yours.
- [Snow White (The Original)](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/snow-white-the-original/): Envy eats you alive.
- [The Pied Piper of Hamelin](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-pied-piper-of-hamelin/): Pay what you owe, or pay more later.
- [The Bremen Town Musicians](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-bremen-town-musicians/): Never write off the old. Together, they still have teeth.
- [The Gingerbread Man](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-gingerbread-man/): Boasting will not make you faster. Only louder.
- [Hans in Luck](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/hans-in-luck/): A fool and his gold soon part, and he calls it luck.
- [Humpty Dumpty](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/humpty-dumpty/): Some things cannot be put back together.
- [The Emperor’s New Clothes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-emperors-new-clothes/): Say the true thing, even when the whole street will not.
- [King Midas](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/king-midas/): Gold is cold, and it never hugs you back.
- [Johnny Head-in-Air](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/johnny-head-in-air/): Look where you are going, or go where you are not looking.
- [Harriet and the Matches](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/harriet-and-the-matches/): Some toys play back.
- [Icarus](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/icarus/): Listen to the warning. The sun will not give you another.
- [The Swineherd](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/the-swineherd/): Turn up your nose at the real thing, and you will be left holding a rattle.
- [Pandora’s Box](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-everyone-knows/pandoras-box/): Some things, once let out, never go back in.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Britain and Ireland (coming soon)

- [The Lake Maiden of Myddfai](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-lake-maiden-of-myddfai/): Keep a promise on bad days too, not just easy ones.
- [Fairy Ointment](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/fairy-ointment/): Medicine meant for someone else is never meant for you.
- [The Field of Boliauns](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-field-of-boliauns/): Grab for easy gold, and you’ll be digging forever.
- [The Small People’s Cow](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-small-peoples-cow/): Grudge others their share, and you’ll lose the whole cow.
- [Kate Crackernuts](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/kate-crackernuts/): Stand by your sister in trouble, and keep your eyes open.
- [The Miser on the Gump](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-miser-on-the-gump/): Sneak up to steal, and you’ll be the one who’s caught.
- [The Pwca’s Supper](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-pwcas-supper/): Don’t eat what was left for someone else. They notice.
- [The Brownie o’ Ferne-Den](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-brownie-o-ferne-den/): Judge folk by what they do, not how they look.
- [The Knockers’ Tenth](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-knockers-tenth/): A bargain’s a bargain, even when nobody is watching.
- [My Own Self](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/my-own-self/): Poke the fire after bedtime, and somebody gets burned.
- [The White Cow of Llyn Barfog](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-white-cow-of-llyn-barfog/): Be grateful for a gift, or greed will send it home.
- [The Fairies of Merlin’s Crag](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-fairies-of-merlins-crag/): If you know it’s wrong, don’t do it because someone laughs.
- [The Seal Hunter’s Oath](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-seal-hunters-oath/): The creature you hurt has a family waiting for it.
- [Tamlane](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/tamlane/): Hold on to a friend in trouble, however scary it gets.
- [Mr Miacca](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/mr-miacca/): Stay where your grown-ups can see you.
- [The Horned Women](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-horned-women/): Open your door at midnight, and twelve come in.
- [The Kelpie’s Bridle](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-kelpies-bridle/): A horse that wants you on its back has plans.
- [The Hedley Kow](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-hedley-kow/): Make the best of what you get, and every change is luck.
- [The Moddey Dhoo](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-moddey-dhoo/): Never go into danger on a dare just to look brave.
- [The Red Etin](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-red-etin/): Share what you have, and you’ll have help when you need it.
- [Selena Moor](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/selena-moor/): Never eat fruit you don’t know, however ripe it looks.
- [Vengeance Cometh](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/vengeance-cometh/): Spoil what others love, and you’ll lose what you love.
- [The Buggane of St Trinian’s](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-buggane-of-st-trinians/): Finish the job before the monster finishes climbing.
- [Childe Rowland](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/childe-rowland/): Hold on to good advice most when you’re hungry and tempted.
- [Tehi Tegi](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/tehi-tegi/): Don’t follow a crowd into water. It’s deeper than it looks.
- [The Black Bull of Norroway](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-black-bull-of-norroway/): Lost something by one slip? Keep going till you win it back.
- [Canonbie Dick](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/canonbie-dick/): Do the hard, brave part first, not the easy, noisy one.
- [The Golden Arm](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-golden-arm/): Love the person, not the gold they’ve got.
- [How the Herring Became King](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/how-the-herring-became-king/): Be plain, honest and on time. Paint and primping lose.
- [The Salmon of Knowledge](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-salmon-of-knowledge/): Tell the truth about an accident. Honest people will be fair.
- [The Cormorant and the Bat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-cormorant-and-the-bat/): Break your word in the storm, and hide forever after.
- [The Hound of Culann](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-hound-of-culann/): Break something precious, and stand guard in its place.
- [King O’Toole and His Goose](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/king-otoole-and-his-goose/): Keep your word, even when it costs the last acre.
- [Fionn’s Wife and the Giant](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/fionns-wife-and-the-giant/): Brains beat bullies. Think first, and you won’t need fists.
- [Whittington and His Cat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/whittington-and-his-cat/): About to give up? Stop, listen, and turn again.
- [The Well of Fior Usga](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-well-of-fior-usga/): Lock up what should be shared, and it drowns you.
- [The Laidly Worm](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-laidly-worm/): Lower your sword and listen. The monster might be family.
- [The Drowned Hundred](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-drowned-hundred/): Do the job first. “One more” can sink a whole country.
- [Cap o’ Rushes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/cap-o-rushes/): Honest love is salt: plain, but you can’t do without it.
- [The Lambton Worm](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-britain-and-ireland/the-lambton-worm/): Throw your trouble down a well, and it grows.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of France & the Low Countries (coming soon)

- [Bruin and the Honey-Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/bruin-and-the-honey-tree/): When a liar offers you a treat, keep your head out.
- [Tybert in the Priest’s Barn](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/tybert-in-the-priests-barn/): When a liar points you to dinner, ask who set the table.
- [The Price Written on the Hoof](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-price-written-on-the-hoof/): Boast you can read anything, and a hoof will teach you.
- [Drakestail](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/drakestail/): Pay back what you borrow. Little lenders have big friends.
- [The Blackbird and the Fox](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-blackbird-and-the-fox/): A fox who says he’s changed is still a fox.
- [The Sick Wolf](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-sick-wolf/): Don’t fool yourself about how much is enough.
- [The Wolf, the Snail and the Wasps](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-wolf-the-snail-and-the-wasps/): Trample the small, and the small will be waiting.
- [The Two Goats](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-two-goats/): Two who won’t step back both go down.
- [The Monkey and the Cat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-monkey-and-the-cat/): If someone flatters you into the risky part, say no.
- [The Wolf in the Pear Oven](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-wolf-in-the-pear-oven/): A fox’s excuse works once. The farmer has heard it.
- [The Mouse Who Asked Nicely](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-mouse-who-asked-nicely/): Stay out of reach. You can’t always talk your way out.
- [The Heron Who Waited for Better](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-heron-who-waited-for-better/): Sniff at good enough, and you’ll end up glad of a snail.
- [Monsieur Seguin’s Goat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/monsieur-seguins-goat/): Run off where nobody can hear you, and nobody can help.
- [When the Long Winter Came](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/when-the-long-winter-came/): Anyone can say “That’s me.” Ask before you hand it over.
- [Weather to Order](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/weather-to-order/): Order sunshine every single day, and you’ll harvest empty ears.
- [The Divided Horse-Cloth](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-divided-horse-cloth/): Be kind to the old. One day, you will be old too.
- [The Bird Who Kept the Orchard](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-bird-who-kept-the-orchard/): What’s good in your hand, never throw away.
- [A Lost Paradise](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/a-lost-paradise/): Blame others for prying, and you’ll be the first to peek.
- [Misère and the Walnut Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/mis-re-and-the-walnut-tree/): When someone wise says, “Ask for what matters,” listen.
- [Beauty and the Beast](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/beauty-and-the-beast/): Envy turns you to stone, and leaves you watching.
- [Prince Darling](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/prince-darling/): Every cruelty grows on you. Eventually it shows.
- [The Fair One with Golden Locks](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-fair-one-with-golden-locks/): Help the small ones you meet. One day you’ll need them.
- [The Three Wishes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-three-wishes/): Wish in anger, and you’ll spend the rest undoing it.
- [Bellah and the Groac’h](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/bellah-and-the-groach/): Forget your true friend for a stranger’s gold, and you’ll need rescuing.
- [Blondine](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/blondine/): When someone says, “Don’t tell,” that’s exactly when to tell.
- [The Lady of Stavoren](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-lady-of-stavoren/): What you waste in pride, you will beg for in rags.
- [The Drowned City of Ys](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-drowned-city-of-ys/): Let a flatterer near the key, and the flood comes for you.
- [The Stones of Plouhinec](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-stones-of-plouhinec/): When someone offers easy gold, ask what they aren’t telling you.
- [The Palace Under the Dunes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-palace-under-the-dunes/): When it’s time to get out, get out. Leave the treasure.
- [The Piper and the Korrigans](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-piper-and-the-korrigans/): When people who know the place warn you, listen.
- [Teuz and the Ashes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/teuz-and-the-ashes/): Burn your helpers’ feet, and you’ll do the work yourself.
- [The Siren of La Fresnaye](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-siren-of-la-fresnaye/): Let the wild thing go home. Kindness comes back on the tide.
- [The White Inn](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-white-inn/): When someone needs help, ask what they need. Then do it.
- [The Ghost’s Supper](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-ghosts-supper/): Scare people for fun, and the fright comes back to you.
- [The Landmark Removed](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-landmark-removed/): Move your neighbour’s fence, and carry it forever.
- [Kludde](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/kludde/): Never jump on a ride you don’t know.
- [The Fiddler Tricked](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-fiddler-tricked/): If a stranger’s offer sounds too good, it isn’t real.
- [The Three Water-Maidens of Jupille](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-three-water-maidens-of-jupille/): Give back what’s someone else’s the moment they ask.
- [Melusina of the Bock](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/melusina-of-the-bock/): Break the one promise, and lose everything it protected.
- [The Flying Dutchman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-france-and-the-low-countries/the-flying-dutchman/): In a storm, turning back isn’t giving up. It’s sense.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of the German Lands (coming soon)

- [Cat and Mouse in Partnership](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/cat-and-mouse-in-partnership/): Keep your fat away from anyone with claws.
- [Mouse, Bird and Sausage](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/mouse-bird-and-sausage/): Trade a job that works for a grumble, and nobody comes home.
- [Straw, Coal and Bean](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/straw-coal-and-bean/): Laugh at a friend’s fall, and you’ll split.
- [The Wolf and the Fox](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-wolf-and-the-fox/): Eat till you don’t fit the door, and you stay.
- [The Fox and the Cat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-fox-and-the-cat/): One trick you know beats a hundred you brag about.
- [The Wren and the Bear](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-wren-and-the-bear/): Sneer at small children, and their whole family comes.
- [The Dog and the Sparrow](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-dog-and-the-sparrow/): Be cruel to the small, and the small will ruin you.
- [The Ungrateful Son](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-ungrateful-son/): Hide your supper from your father, and it finds your face.
- [Sweet Porridge](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/sweet-porridge/): Learn the “stop” before you say the “go.”
- [Clever Elsie](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/clever-elsie/): Worry about tomorrow, and you’ll lose today, then yourself.
- [Frau Trude](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/frau-trude/): When the people who love you say “don’t go,” don’t go.
- [The Little Folks’ Presents](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-little-folks-presents/): Take a gift twice, and lose it twice.
- [Simeli Mountain](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/simeli-mountain/): Greed remembers the gold and forgets the way out.
- [The Cudgel in the Sack](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-cudgel-in-the-sack/): Rob a guest, and his luggage may rob you back.
- [The Devil’s Three Golden Hairs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-devils-three-golden-hairs/): Chase another man’s luck, and you’ll row his boat forever.
- [Godfather Death](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/godfather-death/): Cheat Death once, and he counts it. Twice, he collects.
- [The Heinzelmännchen of Cologne](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-heinzelm-nnchen-of-cologne/): Spy on a kindness, and it leaves for good.
- [The Innkeeper’s Wine](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-innkeepers-wine/): Water your wine, and the river will tell on you.
- [The Lorelei](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-lorelei/): Watch the river, not the song.
- [The Seven Sisters of Schönberg](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-seven-sisters-of-sch-nberg/): Make sport of hearts, and the river makes stones of you.
- [The Mouse Tower of Bingen](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-mouse-tower-of-bingen/): Call the hungry mice, and the mice will come.
- [The Judge and the Devil](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-judge-and-the-devil/): A curse meant in earnest finds its address.
- [Bread Turned to Stone](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/bread-turned-to-stone/): Wish stone on the hungry, and eat stone yourself.
- [The Wild Huntsman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-wild-huntsman/): Jeer at the Wild Hunt, and you’ll share the kill.
- [The Horse’s Leap](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-horses-leap/): Win twice, then stop. The third time is the gorge’s.
- [The Wonder-Flower](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-wonder-flower/): Grab the shiny things, and you’ll drop the one that mattered.
- [The Moss-Woman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-moss-woman/): When the little folk ask a small thing, do it.
- [The Cold Heart](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-cold-heart/): Trade your heart for gold, and you’ll feel nothing, not even regret.
- [The Boundary Race](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-boundary-race/): A pampered rooster sleeps through the morning that matters.
- [The Devil’s Bridge](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-devils-bridge/): Make a deal with the Devil, and read the small print first.
- [The Alphorn](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-alphorn/): Choose the gift you love, not the one you’d brag about.
- [The Chamois Hunter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-chamois-hunter/): Take the gift, keep the promise. Not one more shot.
- [Earth in His Shoes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/earth-in-his-shoes/): Lie with your feet, and your feet will never rest.
- [The Cheese Staircase](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-cheese-staircase/): Pave your stairs with plenty, and the mountain buries the lot.
- [The Golden Pears](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-golden-pears/): Say what’s really in your basket.
- [The Two Golden Chains](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-two-golden-chains/): Let go of one gold chain for two, and hold nothing.
- [The Gold-Measurers of Lofer](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-gold-measurers-of-lofer/): Cheat the one who can’t see, and you’ll guard it forever.
- [The Sunken Forest](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-sunken-forest/): Never say “let it sink” about something you stole.
- [Frau Hütt](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/frau-h-tt/): Scrub with bread, and you’ll stand in stone.
- [The Giant Serles](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-german-lands/the-giant-serles/): Hunt over other people’s lives, and you’ll stand still forever.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of the Nordic Lands (coming soon)

- [Gefjun Ploughs Away a Kingdom](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/gefjun-ploughs-away-a-kingdom/): Promise carelessly, and someone will plough off with your kingdom.
- [The Builder of Asgard’s Wall](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-builder-of-asgards-wall/): Ask for the sun and moon, and you may get the hammer.
- [Thor’s Goats](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/thors-goats/): Break one small rule, and pay with something large.
- [Thor and Utgarda-Loki](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/thor-and-utgarda-loki/): However strong you are, Old Age wins the wrestling.
- [Idunn’s Apples](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/idunns-apples/): Sell out a friend, and you’ll be sent to fetch her back.
- [Alvis the All-Knowing](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/alvis-the-all-knowing/): Love your own voice, and the sun will catch you talking.
- [Sif’s Hair and Loki’s Wager](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/sifs-hair-and-lokis-wager/): Bet your head, and someone will come to collect.
- [Hrungnir’s Boast](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/hrungnirs-boast/): Boast in another man’s hall, and you’ll answer for it.
- [The Otter’s Ransom](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-otters-ransom/): Squeeze out the last ring, and the curse comes with it.
- [Thrym Steals the Hammer](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/thrym-steals-the-hammer/): Take what isn’t yours, and expect it back at the wedding.
- [The Binding of Fenrir](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-binding-of-fenrir/): A promise backed by a lie costs somebody a hand.
- [The Guest Between the Fires](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-guest-between-the-fires/): Be cruel to a stranger. He may be a god.
- [The One Who Would Not Weep](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-one-who-would-not-weep/): One hard heart can keep the whole world grieving.
- [Why the Sea Is Salt](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/why-the-sea-is-salt/): Greed buys the mill, but never asks how to stop it.
- [The Husband Who Minded the House](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-husband-who-minded-the-house/): Call her work easy, and spend the evening up the chimney.
- [Gertrude’s Bird](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/gertrudes-bird/): Grudge a hungry man a crumb, and hunt crumbs forever.
- [Why the Bear Has a Stumpy Tail](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/why-the-bear-has-a-stumpy-tail/): Believe the fox with the stolen fish, and lose your tail.
- [Nail Soup](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/nail-soup/): Lie to a guest about your larder, and he’ll empty it politely.
- [Well Done and Ill Paid](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/well-done-and-ill-paid/): Cheat the one who helped you, and get no help next time.
- [Kitta Grau and the Evil One](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/kitta-grau-and-the-evil-one/): A wagging tongue can do what the Evil One cannot.
- [The Cat on the Dovrefell](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-cat-on-the-dovrefell/): Poke the big cat, and you’ll never be invited back.
- [The Trolls in Hedale Wood](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-trolls-in-hedale-wood/): Hunt children in the dark, and you may lose your only eye.
- [The Giant Who Hid His Heart](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-giant-who-hid-his-heart/): Hide your heart far away, and someone will travel there.
- [St Peter and the Two Women](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/st-peter-and-the-two-women/): Copy a gift out of greed, and it turns into a curse.
- [The Boy Who Scared the Stallo](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-boy-who-scared-the-stallo/): Caught by a bully? Keep calm, and find what frightens him.
- [Yuletide Specters](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/yuletide-specters/): Race to be first, and you may arrive among the dead.
- [The Lady of Pintorp](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-lady-of-pintorp/): Grind down the poor, and a stranger’s coach will come for you.
- [The Girl Who Stepped on Bread](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-girl-who-stepped-on-bread/): Step on bread to save your shoes, and lose everything else.
- [The Wonderful Pot](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-wonderful-pot/): Grab what isn’t yours, and it may carry you off.
- [The Merman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-merman/): Mind what you kick, what you curse, and whom you trust.
- [The Stallo’s Shy Bride](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-stallos-shy-bride/): Rush out in a rage, and the cold will catch you first.
- [The Singing Contest](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-singing-contest/): Boast at an old singer, and you’ll sing from the swamp.
- [The Nisse Who Killed the Cow](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-nisse-who-killed-the-cow/): Finish your porridge before you take your revenge.
- [The Silver Dish](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-silver-dish/): Blame Adam and Eve, then lift the lid yourself.
- [The Fir Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-fir-tree/): Wish your life away, and you’ll get your wish.
- [The Wolf Sings](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-wolf-sings/): Fill your belly in a stranger’s house, then keep your mouth shut.
- [The Mermaid’s Reward](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-mermaids-reward/): Leave be what does you no harm, and your luck stays.
- [The Wild Animals and the Tame Ones](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-wild-animals-and-the-tame-ones/): Refuse good advice, and you’ll pull someone else’s sledge forever.
- [The Raven of Skíðastaðir](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-raven-of-sk-asta-ir/): Work your servants without rest, and the mountain will rest on you.
- [The Giant’s Three Gifts](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-nordic-lands/the-giants-three-gifts/): Mock a gift, and it may stop coming.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of the Baltic (coming soon)

- [The Orphan’s Handmill](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-orphans-handmill/): Steal the gift meant for someone else, and it burns you.
- [The Dwarf’s Christening](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-dwarfs-christening/): Hurt something small and helpless, and the hurt comes back.
- [The Faithless Fisherman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-faithless-fisherman/): Cheat the partner who fills your nets, and the nets stay empty.
- [The Man in Bast Shoes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-man-in-bast-shoes/): Every trick you play waits for you further down the road.
- [The Miser’s Wooden Servants](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-misers-wooden-servants/): Treat your helpers fairly, or you’ll end up with no one.
- [Tiidu the Piper](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/tiidu-the-piper/): Don’t forget your family while you chase the gold.
- [The Spider and the Hornet](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-spider-and-the-hornet/): Lie to the judge, and you’ll wear your lie forever.
- [The Spirit of the Whirlwind](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-spirit-of-the-whirlwind/): Laugh off good advice, and the storm will teach you.
- [The Treasure at Kärdla](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-treasure-at-k-rdla/): Some work must be done with your mouth shut.
- [The Old Man of Lake Ülemiste](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-old-man-of-lake-lemiste/): Never boast you’re finished. There’s always more to do.
- [The Woodcutter’s Golden Rod](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-woodcutters-golden-rod/): Ask for what can be; reach for the sun, and burn.
- [Emmu Lake and Virts Lake](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/emmu-lake-and-virts-lake/): Spoil the spring, and drink from puddles.
- [The Ice Roof of the Lake](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-ice-roof-of-the-lake/): Wait till the ice is thick; the lake keeps whoever hurries.
- [How the Animals Dug the Daugava](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/how-the-animals-dug-the-daugava/): Skip the digging, and you’ll beg the sky for water.
- [The Fox and the Jug](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-fox-and-the-jug/): Lose your temper when you’re stuck, and you sink deeper.
- [The Crane Who Taught the Fox to Fly](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-crane-who-taught-the-fox-to-fly/): Before you ask to fly, ask how you’ll land.
- [The Hare Who Laughed](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-hare-who-laughed/): Laugh at someone more frightened, and it marks your face.
- [The Catfish and the Burbot](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-catfish-and-the-burbot/): Don’t believe every gloomy story. Go and look yourself.
- [The Fox and the Thrush](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-fox-and-the-thrush/): A tail is not an axe, however loudly you say it.
- [The Cuckoo and the Deaf Ploughman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-cuckoo-and-the-deaf-ploughman/): Mock the old man’s ears, and you’ll repeat yourself forever.
- [The Owl Who Would Not Learn](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-owl-who-would-not-learn/): Do the learning first. A full belly makes a sleepy head.
- [Why the Wolf’s Mouth Is Black](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/why-the-wolfs-mouth-is-black/): Cheat the one who works for you, and he’ll pay himself.
- [The Horse Who Was Too Busy](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-horse-who-was-too-busy/): Too busy to help? Then you’ll work and never be full.
- [The Miller Who Played the Bear](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-miller-who-played-the-bear/): Play the bear to scare an old man, and stay a bear.
- [The Pot That Was Too Full](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-pot-that-was-too-full/): Grumble at a gift, and you’ll keep only half of it.
- [Laima’s Shoes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/laimas-shoes/): Keep the promise you made before your luck came.
- [Why Nobody Knows Their Last Day](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/why-nobody-knows-their-last-day/): Don’t wreck what you can’t take; someone comes after you.
- [The Thrush Who Didn’t Give It Back](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-thrush-who-didnt-give-it-back/): Borrow it, return it, or it follows you to the party.
- [The Wolf Who Wanted to Bake Bread](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-wolf-who-wanted-to-bake-bread/): Want the loaf without the work, and you’ll go without.
- [The Owl on Watch](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-owl-on-watch/): Fall asleep on watch, and you’ll never show your face by day.
- [The Heron and the Crane](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-heron-and-the-crane/): Say no out of pride, yes too late, and you’ll walk forever.
- [The Goat Who Lied](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-goat-who-lied/): Lie to get others in trouble, and it comes back on you.
- [Why the Stork’s Back Is Black](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/why-the-storks-back-is-black/): Finish the job you were trusted with before you peek.
- [The King Who Picked Up Three Pennies](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-king-who-picked-up-three-pennies/): Laugh at a small coin, and eat your dinner without salt.
- [The Crayfish Who Wanted Eyes Behind](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-crayfish-who-wanted-eyes-behind/): Ask for help to cheat, and you’ll walk backwards all your life.
- [The Man Who Gave Away His Belly](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-man-who-gave-away-his-belly/): Your work feeds you. Wish it away, and your strength goes too.
- [The Rich Meadow and the Poor Bog](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-rich-meadow-and-the-poor-bog/): Boast that you did it alone, and watch it stop growing.
- [The Old Man’s Night’s Lodging](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-old-mans-nights-lodging/): Be kind only to get something, and you’ll get fleas.
- [The Night Spinners](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-night-spinners/): Don’t let strangers in at night; if you did, run for help.
- [The Cat and the Sparrow](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-baltic/the-cat-and-the-sparrow/): Caught? Keep your head, and wait for your chance to fly.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of the Slavic Lands (coming soon)

- [Morozko](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/morozko/): Mind your manners in the cold. The cold is listening.
- [Vasilisa the Beautiful](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/vasilisa-the-beautiful/): Send a girl to Baba Yaga, and Baba Yaga sends something back.
- [Teremok](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/teremok/): A house with room for everyone has room for the bear.
- [The Bear and the Basket of Pies](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-bear-and-the-basket-of-pies/): Clever beats big, especially when big wants pie.
- [Sister Alyonushka and Brother Ivanushka](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/sister-alyonushka-and-brother-ivanushka/): Wait for the well, however thirsty you are.
- [The Leshy](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-leshy/): Go into the woods without asking, and the woods may keep you.
- [The Nanny-Goat in the Nut Grove](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-nanny-goat-in-the-nut-grove/): Come home when you’re called, before somebody sends the wolves.
- [The Snow Daughter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-snow-daughter/): Grudge your helper a hen, and lose what you love.
- [The Bear’s Paw](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-bears-paw/): Take from the forest, and the forest comes to collect.
- [One-Eyed Likho](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/one-eyed-likho/): Go looking for trouble, and it will find you first.
- [Sozh and Dnieper](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/sozh-and-dnieper/): Try to win by a trick, and you’ll serve the winner.
- [The Frog Tsarevna](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-frog-tsarevna/): Burn the skin in a hurry, search the world at leisure.
- [Marya Morevna](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/marya-morevna/): The one door you’re told to leave shut, leave shut.
- [The Mitten](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-mitten/): Too many in one small mitten, and the hunter notices.
- [The Straw Ox](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-straw-ox/): Steal a lick of someone’s tar, and you’ll pay in honey.
- [Sirko](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/sirko/): Don’t throw out the old dog. He still has teeth.
- [The Old Father Goes to School](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-old-father-goes-to-school/): Treat your father as you’d want your children to treat you.
- [The Good Sons](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-good-sons/): Keep your elders close. One day you’ll need what they know.
- [The Dragon of Wawel](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-dragon-of-wawel/): Gulp without looking, and one day you’ll swallow fire.
- [The Pale Maiden](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-pale-maiden/): Squeeze the poor, and Poverty comes to live with you.
- [The Twelve Months](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-twelve-months/): Ask winter for summer’s fruit, and winter will answer.
- [Budulínek](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/budul-nek/): Don’t open the door, whatever they promise you.
- [The Disobedient Rooster](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-disobedient-rooster/): Thin ice doesn’t care how much you wanted to slide.
- [The Wood Maiden](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-wood-maiden/): Don’t throw away a gift because it looks like leaves.
- [The Jezinkas](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-jezinkas/): Refuse the stranger’s apple, however rosy.
- [Carried Off by the Wind](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/carried-off-by-the-wind/): Curse a man to the wind, and the wind learns your name.
- [Three Times “God Reward You”](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/three-times-god-reward-you/): Never laugh at a thank-you. It weighs more than you think.
- [Batcha and the Serpent King](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/batcha-and-the-serpent-king/): Swear to keep a secret, then keep it.
- [Twardowski](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/twardowski/): Make a bargain with a devil, and read the small print.
- [The Lord God as an Old Man](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-lord-god-as-an-old-man/): Refuse a thirsty stranger, and chase your cows till dark.
- [The Old Wolf and His Three Suppers](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-old-wolf-and-his-three-suppers/): Want to be flattered more than fed, and you’ll get neither.
- [Wiser than the Tsar](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/wiser-than-the-tsar/): Send away the wise, and they’ll take you with them.
- [The Hare That Ran into the Mill](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-hare-that-ran-into-the-mill/): When the prize runs into a dark place, let it go.
- [The Vila](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-vila/): Keep the one promise she asked of you.
- [The She-Wolf](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-she-wolf/): What you keep by theft walks out when it’s found.
- [The White Snake](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/the-white-snake/): A small lie can burn the one who trusted you.
- [Fate](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/fate/): Call borrowed luck “mine,” and watch it burn.
- [God’s Cock](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/gods-cock/): Ignore the only warning you got, and the lake comes.
- [Fisherman Palunko and His Wife](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/fisherman-palunko-and-his-wife/): Chase the Sea King’s gold, and you’ll end up his fool.
- [Stribor’s Forest](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-slavic-lands/stribors-forest/): Marry for a pretty face, and your mother pays.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of the Carpathians (coming soon)

- [The Golden-Fleeced Lamb](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-golden-fleeced-lamb/): Grab what isn’t yours, and you’ll dance for everyone to see.
- [The Little Dumpling](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-little-dumpling/): Swallow more than you can hold, and you’ll burst.
- [The Reward of Boasting](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-reward-of-boasting/): Boast you need nothing, and that’s what you’ll inherit.
- [The Little Hen and the Sloe](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-little-hen-and-the-sloe/): Haggle while someone’s choking, and your help comes too late.
- [Luck and Bliss](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/luck-and-bliss/): The best help lets someone stand on their own feet.
- [The Student and the Loaf](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-student-and-the-loaf/): Hard work takes patience. Rage only makes you burst.
- [Truth and Falsehood](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/truth-and-falsehood/): Don’t hand a sweet-talker everything first. Liars don’t pay back.
- [The Castle of Luck](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-castle-of-luck/): When the good chance calls, go now. Noon won’t wait.
- [The Emperor Who Said There Was No God](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-emperor-who-said-there-was-no-god/): Think nobody’s above you, and your own gate won’t know you.
- [The King and the Two Maidens](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-king-and-the-two-maidens/): Treat the plain coat like the king’s. You can’t see who’s inside.
- [The Just Wage](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-just-wage/): Do the work well and be kind to small things.
- [Two Neighbours and Their Sheep](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/two-neighbours-and-their-sheep/): Give only to get a hundred back, and you’ll wake to bones.
- [The Duckling’s Journey](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-ducklings-journey/): Before you ride on someone’s back, ask if they dive.
- [The Nightingale and the Turtle-Dove](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-nightingale-and-the-turtle-dove/): Sleep through the lesson, and you’ll sing one note for life.
- [The Nightingale at the King’s Table](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-nightingale-at-the-kings-table/): Don’t judge the singer by her feathers.
- [The Titmouse Who Didn’t Wait](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-titmouse-who-didnt-wait/): Hear the whole answer before you fly off with half.
- [The Cuckoo’s Broken Promise](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-cuckoos-broken-promise/): Promise only what you’ll do. A broken promise makes you hide.
- [The Nosy Old Woman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-nosy-old-woman/): Poke your nose in every pot, and you’ll peck forever.
- [The Hornet’s Cardboard Gift](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-hornets-cardboard-gift/): Bring a fake gift, and your own work turns to paper.
- [The Bee and the Spider](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-bee-and-the-spider/): When someone you love needs you, drop the bricks and run.
- [Why the Stork Has No Tail](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/why-the-stork-has-no-tail/): Mock the one who did the hard thing? Check your own tail.
- [The Stork and the Tomtit](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-stork-and-the-tomtit/): Pretend to be what you’re not, and one boast gives you away.
- [The Hoopoe Who Wanted Better](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-hoopoe-who-wanted-better/): Turn down good food, and you’ll eat what others leave behind.
- [The Late Thistle-Finch](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-late-thistle-finch/): Late for a true reason? Say so. Truth gets the last colours.
- [The Maize Loaf and the Wheat Loaf](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-maize-loaf-and-the-wheat-loaf/): Greet with an insult, get one back. Give respect, get respect.
- [The Girl Who Spun from the Rubbish](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-girl-who-spun-from-the-rubbish/): Throw good wool away, and someone else will spin it.
- [The Gad-Fly and the Lazy Cowherd](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-gad-fly-and-the-lazy-cowherd/): Answer politely, even when you’re tired. Rudeness runs off with the herd.
- [The Woman Who Hid the Loaf](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-woman-who-hid-the-loaf/): Hide from a promise, and you’ll carry your hiding place forever.
- [The Sower’s Wheat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-sowers-wheat/): Help someone in trouble. Even the plain truth can shelter them.
- [The Boastful Thrush](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-boastful-thrush/): Don’t brag that summer’s here. March still has snow in it.
- [Baba Dochia](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/baba-dochia/): Cruel to others and careless with the weather? March will find you.
- [The Rich Man’s Granary](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-rich-mans-granary/): Hoard bread while neighbours starve, and the weevils eat first.
- [The Wolf Who Would Be Mayor](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-wolf-who-would-be-mayor/): If someone offers dinner for no work, it’s a trap.
- [The Lazy Dog](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-lazy-dog/): Build your shelter on the warm day, not the freezing one.
- [The Goat and the Snake](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-goat-and-the-snake/): A friend who squeezes your neck is no friend. Get free first.
- [The Stingy Farmer’s Stable](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-stingy-farmers-stable/): Share the little you have. The stingy wake to an empty stable.
- [The Son Who Turned His Mother Away](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-son-who-turned-his-mother-away/): Grow as big as you like. Never be ashamed of your mother.
- [The Steward’s Work-Party](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-stewards-work-party/): Try to get something for nothing, and it costs double.
- [The Carter Who Answered to His Name](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-carter-who-answered-to-his-name/): Beware the one who scares you, then offers to hold your things.
- [The Rat Who Went to Find God](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-carpathians/the-rat-who-went-to-find-god/): Puff yourself up, and the wind will put you down.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Italy (coming soon)

- [Cola Pesce](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/cola-pesce/): Know when to say no, even to a king.
- [Catherine and Her Fate](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/catherine-and-her-fate/): Do the hard part first. The good part will keep.
- [Firrazzanu and the Deaf Queen](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/firrazzanu-and-the-deaf-queen/): A trick that makes others look silly soon makes you look sillier.
- [The Abbot Who Had Nothing to Think About](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-abbot-who-had-nothing-to-think-about/): Boast of having nothing to think about, and you’ll be given something.
- [Giufà and the Fly on the Judge’s Nose](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/giuf-and-the-fly-on-the-judges-nose/): Say exactly what you mean. Someone may do exactly that.
- [The Man With One Bean](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-man-with-one-bean/): Trade a bean for the world, and the world bites back.
- [The Doctor’s Apprentice](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-doctors-apprentice/): Copy a master’s trick without his wits, and look a fool.
- [One Hundred Looks at the King](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/one-hundred-looks-at-the-king/): Care for your parents. They cared for you first.
- [The Cock Who Wanted to Be Pope](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-cock-who-wanted-to-be-pope/): Crow too high, and you’ll end up in the pot.
- [The Stones and the Bread](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-stones-and-the-bread/): Carry your share honestly, not only when you think it pays.
- [St Peter’s Mother and the Leek Leaf](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/st-peters-mother-and-the-leek-leaf/): Pull others up with you, or you’ll fall alone.
- [The Girl Who Ate Only Sweets](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-girl-who-ate-only-sweets/): Eat real food first. Sweets can’t keep you going.
- [The Story Without “Once Upon a Time”](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-story-without-once-upon-a-time/): Set a trap with words, and mind your own.
- [Michele Fico Forgets His Name](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/michele-fico-forgets-his-name/): Don’t open the door until you know who’s knocking.
- [Fra Ignazio’s Saddlebags](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/fra-ignazios-saddlebags/): A gift squeezed from the poor is no gift at all.
- [Godfather Wolf’s Frying Pan](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/godfather-wolfs-frying-pan/): Eat what isn’t yours, then lie about it, and trouble knocks.
- [Twelve Feet of Nose](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/twelve-feet-of-nose/): Cheat a simple man, and wear it on your face.
- [The Old Miser Who Wanted a Wife Who Lived on Air](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-old-miser-who-wanted-a-wife-who-lived-on-air/): Too stingy to share? You’ll be fooled out of far more.
- [The Beggar’s Ewe](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-beggars-ewe/): Give a guest your best, even when your best is small.
- [The Spoon in St Peter’s Bag](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-spoon-in-st-peters-bag/): Plant the blame on someone else, and it lands on you.
- [St Peter and the Ham](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/st-peter-and-the-ham/): Found something? Ask out loud whose it is, not in a whisper.
- [St Peter and the Missing Liver](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/st-peter-and-the-missing-liver/): Eat it in secret, and even an ant will tell on you.
- [The Cat Who Was Not Thanked](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-cat-who-was-not-thanked/): A favour forgotten is a friend lost.
- [Goat-Face](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/goat-face/): Say thank you to the one who helped you up.
- [The Months](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-months/): A kind word costs nothing; a sour one costs plenty.
- [Truthful Joseph](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/truthful-joseph/): The truth is cheaper to keep than a lie.
- [Buchettino](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/buchettino/): Never hand a stranger anything with your own hand.
- [The Wolf and the Crab](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-wolf-and-the-crab/): Mock someone’s crooked walk, and they may still beat you.
- [The Share of the Lashes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-share-of-the-lashes/): Demand a share of someone’s reward, and you’ll share the price.
- [Pomo and the Black Horse](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/pomo-and-the-black-horse/): Never pretend you can fix someone who’s hurt. Get help.
- [March and the Shepherd](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/march-and-the-shepherd/): Don’t boast the storm is over until it truly is.
- [The Blind Man and the Fig Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-blind-man-and-the-fig-tree/): Take what isn’t yours, and greed will make you give it back.
- [The Monkey and the Watered Wine](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-monkey-and-the-watered-wine/): Cheat by half, and you’ll lose by half.
- [The Frying-Pan Wager](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-frying-pan-wager/): Stubbornness over a silly bet costs more than losing it.
- [The Witches’ Figs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-witches-figs/): Rude words turn good figs into nothing.
- [The Boy Who Mocked the Old Woman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-boy-who-mocked-the-old-woman/): Mock the old, and you may ride home in their sack.
- [The Fiddle](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-fiddle/): Plot against the fool, and you’ll dance to his tune.
- [The Enchanted Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-enchanted-tree/): Share your bread with the hungry, however strange they look.
- [The Cobbler Who Killed Flies](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-cobbler-who-killed-flies/): Brag about a deed, and you’ll be asked to do it again.
- [The Language of Animals](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-italy/the-language-of-animals/): Learn what others laugh at. One day it may save you.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Iberia (coming soon)

- [The Mouse with the Blue Ribbon](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-mouse-with-the-blue-ribbon/): A sweet voice can hide a hungry mouth.
- [The Fox’s Harvest](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-foxs-harvest/): No hand in the work, no paw in the harvest.
- [The Rooster Who Took Advice](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-rooster-who-took-advice/): Never trust a friend who asks you to give up your spurs.
- [The Ant and the Goat in the House](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-ant-and-the-goat-in-the-house/): The biggest friends ran away; the smallest one went in.
- [The Rabbit and the Cat’s Tail](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-rabbit-and-the-cats-tail/): Start a quarrel out of spite, and it finishes you both.
- [Why Dogs Sniff](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/why-dogs-sniff/): Fuss at every feast, and someone pays for it forever.
- [The Wolves on Each Other’s Backs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-wolves-on-each-others-backs/): Run out from under your friends, and they’ll come down on you.
- [The Little Ant and Pérez the Mouse](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-little-ant-and-p-rez-the-mouse/): Ignore one warning at the stove, and you’re in the soup.
- [Patufet](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/patufet/): Pick your hiding place with care: oxen eat cabbages.
- [Grain-of-Maize](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/grain-of-maize/): A small voice in the right place can empty a robbers’ den.
- [The Promise at the Door](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-promise-at-the-door/): Keep the door shut, however sad the voice outside.
- [The Singing Sack](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-singing-sack/): Never go back alone for something you left behind.
- [The Granny in the Gourd](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-granny-in-the-gourd/): Don’t lift the lid until you’re home.
- [The Little Box](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-little-box/): Turn your own brother from the door, and luck goes with him.
- [The Horseshoe and the Cherries](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-horseshoe-and-the-cherries/): Too proud to stoop once, you’ll stoop a dozen times.
- [Good Luck Asleep](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/good-luck-asleep/): Haggle over every coin, and luck gives you one.
- [The Price of the Eggs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-price-of-the-eggs/): Six eggs cost six eggs, not a henhouse.
- [The Laborer’s Half](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-laborers-half/): Grab the best half first, and you’ll get the worst.
- [Juan Cigarrón](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/juan-cigarr-n/): Pretend to know everything, and someday you’ll have to.
- [The Man Who Hated Warnings](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-man-who-hated-warnings/): Forbid bad news, and you’ll be the last to hear it.
- [The Clever Lad and the Moneylender](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-clever-lad-and-the-moneylender/): A greedy man will pay anything to see heaven.
- [The Flour and the Wind](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-flour-and-the-wind/): Think about what you’re doing, or supper blows away.
- [The Magic Mouthful](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-magic-mouthful/): A quarrel starves if one mouth stays shut.
- [The Ox Called Rabil](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-ox-called-rabil/): Loyalty that can’t be bought is worth more than a farm.
- [Troubles Young or Old](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/troubles-young-or-old/): Take your troubles young, while your back is strong.
- [Same Measure, Same Weight](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/same-measure-same-weight/): Give back what you borrow as good as you got it.
- [The Lamiña’s Golden Comb](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-lami-as-golden-comb/): Keep what isn’t yours, and the mountain comes to collect.
- [The Bridge at Licq](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-bridge-at-licq/): A bargain made in fear always leaves a stone missing.
- [The Lamiña by the Fire](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-lami-a-by-the-fire/): Burn the guest who brings your luck, and your luck leaves too.
- [The Midwife’s Golden Pear](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-midwifes-golden-pear/): Grab for more than a gift gives, and the gift goes home.
- [The Miller’s Share](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-millers-share/): Sneak past a small fair price, and you’ll pay it all.
- [The Three Truths](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-three-truths/): When you’re cornered, the plain truth is the best way out.
- [The Lady Who Fed the Pigs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-lady-who-fed-the-pigs/): What you throw to the pigs, you may eat with them.
- [The Goblin Hen](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-goblin-hen/): Starve the hen that fed you, and she flies for good.
- [The Goblin Who Kneaded Bread](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-goblin-who-kneaded-bread/): Let someone else do your work, and you forget it’s yours.
- [The Devil’s Age](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-devils-age/): Spend the devil’s money, and you’d better have a clever wife.
- [The Brother in the Witches’ Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-brother-in-the-witches-tree/): Copy a lucky man’s secret, and you’ll pay for his luck.
- [The Witches’ Word](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-witches-word/): Meddle with a witch’s pot, and you’ll wear a donkey’s skin.
- [The Lamiña at the Spring](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/the-lami-a-at-the-spring/): Promise to see it through, and then see it through.
- [Juan Holgado and Death](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-iberia/juan-holgado-and-death/): Death sends warnings; the wise read them.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Greece and Rome (coming soon)

- [Arachne](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/arachne/): Be as clever as you like. Never boast to the gods.
- [Leto and the Frogs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/leto-and-the-frogs/): Muddy the water for others, and you will live in it.
- [Battus the Herdsman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/battus-the-herdsman/): A promise for sale is no promise at all.
- [Salmoneus, the Man Who Played Zeus](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/salmoneus-the-man-who-played-zeus/): Play at being a god, and the real one notices.
- [Narcissus and Echo](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/narcissus-and-echo/): Love only yourself, and you will be left with only yourself.
- [King Midas’s Ears](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/king-midass-ears/): Shout down the judge, and it shows. And secrets grow.
- [Tantalus](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/tantalus/): Steal from the gods’ table, and you will never eat again.
- [Dionysus and the Pirates](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/dionysus-and-the-pirates/): Kidnap a stranger, and you may have seized a god.
- [Laomedon’s Wages](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/laomedons-wages/): Pay what you promised, or pay more later.
- [Erysichthon’s Hunger](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/erysichthons-hunger/): Take from the gods’ grove, and nothing will ever fill you.
- [The Cranes of Ibycus](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/the-cranes-of-ibycus/): A guilty tongue always gives itself away.
- [Phaethon](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/phaethon/): Don’t demand what you can’t hold.
- [Baucis and Philemon](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/baucis-and-philemon/): Every stranger at your door might be the one who matters.
- [Archimedes and the Golden Crown](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/archimedes-and-the-golden-crown/): A cheat can fool the scales. It cannot fool the truth.
- [Atalanta’s Golden Apples](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/atalantas-golden-apples/): Stop for gold, forget your thank-yous, and you lose everything.
- [Bellerophon and Pegasus](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/bellerophon-and-pegasus/): Ride too high, and your own horse will throw you.
- [Orpheus Looks Back](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/orpheus-looks-back/): Patience for one more step is everything.
- [Sisyphus](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/sisyphus/): Cheat death once, and you will push uphill forever.
- [Odysseus and the Cyclops](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/odysseus-and-the-cyclops/): Win quietly. Your name is all a curse needs.
- [The Bag of Winds](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/the-bag-of-winds/): Within sight of home is not home.
- [Circe’s Swine](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/circes-swine/): A free feast from a stranger is never free.
- [The Cattle of the Sun](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/the-cattle-of-the-sun/): A promise kept only on a full stomach isn’t kept.
- [The Boast of Ajax](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/the-boast-of-ajax/): Thank the hand that pulled you out.
- [Solon and Croesus](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/solon-and-croesus/): Call no one happy until the story is over.
- [Damon and Phintias](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/damon-and-phintias/): A true friend keeps his word, even when it costs him.
- [Pyrrhus and the Roof Tile](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/pyrrhus-and-the-roof-tile/): Ask “and then what?” before you march.
- [Tarpeia at the Gate](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/tarpeia-at-the-gate/): Ask a traitor’s price, and you will get it.
- [The Sibylline Books](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/the-sibylline-books/): Stubbornness pays more for less.
- [Horatius at the Bridge](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/horatius-at-the-bridge/): One brave man can hold the gap.
- [Menenius and the Belly](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/menenius-and-the-belly/): Refuse to do your part, and you go hungry too.
- [Cloelia Crosses the River](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/cloelia-crosses-the-river/): Be brave enough to escape, and honest enough to go back.
- [Coriolanus and His Mother](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/coriolanus-and-his-mother/): Pride can beat an army. A mother beats pride.
- [Cincinnatus and the Plough](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/cincinnatus-and-the-plough/): Take power when needed. Hand it back when done.
- [The Schoolmaster of Falerii](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/the-schoolmaster-of-falerii/): Win by treachery, and you have already lost.
- [The Geese of the Capitol](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/the-geese-of-the-capitol/): The ones you feed when it’s hard will save you.
- [Brennus and the Scales](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/brennus-and-the-scales/): Pay a bully once, and he’ll add his sword.
- [The Sword of Damocles](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/the-sword-of-damocles/): Envy the throne, and you’ll get the sword above it.
- [Fabricius and the Poisoner](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/fabricius-and-the-poisoner/): Beat your enemy fairly, or you haven’t beaten him.
- [Regulus Keeps His Word](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/regulus-keeps-his-word/): Your word holds, even when it costs everything.
- [Androcles and the Lion](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-greece-and-rome/androcles-and-the-lion/): Kindness in a cave can save you in an arena.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of the Jewish World (coming soon)

- [The Golem of Prague](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-golem-of-prague/): Make nothing you cannot unmake.
- [The Midwife and the Water King](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-midwife-and-the-water-king/): In a stranger’s hall, ask for little.
- [The Locked Chest](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-locked-chest/): A thief who covets will tell you so himself.
- [The Envious Man and the Greedy Man](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-envious-man-and-the-greedy-man/): Envy will pay any price, even its own eye.
- [The Bird’s Three Lessons](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-birds-three-lessons/): Don’t grieve for what has flown, or believe the impossible.
- [The Devil Who Bought the Newest Thing](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-devil-who-bought-the-newest-thing/): Never sell what you haven’t seen yet.
- [The Oath-Breaker and the Demon Queen](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-oath-breaker-and-the-demon-queen/): Break one promise, and the next one breaks you.
- [Bread upon the Waters](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/bread-upon-the-waters/): A small kindness, done every day, comes back from the deep.
- [The Silver Apples and the Gold](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-silver-apples-and-the-gold/): Learn from the bitter apple, and you’ll know the sweet one.
- [The Dragon of Worms](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-dragon-of-worms/): A brave heart needs a clever coat.
- [Kunz and the King’s Three Questions](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/kunz-and-the-kings-three-questions/): Borrowed wisdom runs out at the first hard question.
- [The Grateful Frog](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-grateful-frog/): Keep your promise to the small, and the small keep theirs.
- [The Money in the Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-money-in-the-tree/): What isn’t yours finds its way home.
- [The Man Who Would Not Swear](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-man-who-would-not-swear/): A promise kept costs much, and pays more.
- [The Golem Who Grew Too Tall](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-golem-who-grew-too-tall/): Let a thing grow too big, and it falls on you.
- [The Wise Men of Chelm](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-wise-men-of-chelm/): Four men’s feet to save the snow from two.
- [Hershele and the Hidden Supper](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/hershele-and-the-hidden-supper/): Hide the supper from a guest, and he’ll season it.
- [The Conjurer’s Pupil](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-conjurers-pupil/): Teach a pupil all your tricks, and he’ll learn your last one.
- [The Mountain That Moved](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-mountain-that-moved/): Push the mountain if you must, but watch your coat.
- [The Teacher’s Goat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-teachers-goat/): Trust your own eyes before a stranger’s word.
- [The Cow in the Loft](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-cow-in-the-loft/): Bring the hay to the cow, not the cow to the hay.
- [The Carp That Was Sentenced](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-carp-that-was-sentenced/): Punish in a temper, and your supper swims away.
- [The Logs That Wanted to Roll](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-logs-that-wanted-to-roll/): Take good advice for the next load, not the last one.
- [The Lane That Was Too Narrow](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-lane-that-was-too-narrow/): Before you pull down a wall, try turning the log.
- [The Night Chelm Burned](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-night-chelm-burned/): In a fire, don’t hold a meeting. Get out and shout.
- [The Cat Who Came to Chelm](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-cat-who-came-to-chelm/): Chase a small trouble with fire, and you’ll burn your own roof.
- [The Bear Who Wanted to Fly](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-bear-who-wanted-to-fly/): Copy the bird’s flight, and you’ll get the bear’s fall.
- [The Fox and the Leopard](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-fox-and-the-leopard/): When a fox offers you paradise, ask why he isn’t living there.
- [The Fox Who Tied Up the Lion](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-fox-who-tied-up-the-lion/): Never let your enemy tie the bandage.
- [The Washerwoman Who Outdid the Devil](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-washerwoman-who-outdid-the-devil/): One whispered lie can set a whole town fighting.
