- [The Judge and the Necklace](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-judge-and-the-necklace/): A thief can fool the judge, but not his own household.
- [Half a Friend](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/half-a-friend/): Count your friends on the night you need them.
- [The Thief’s Pomegranate Seed](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-thiefs-pomegranate-seed/): Before you hang the small thief, check your own pockets.
- [The Lightest, the Sweetest, the Hardest](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-lightest-the-sweetest-the-hardest/): Wise men can read the stars and still miss the obvious.
- [The Merchant Who Tried to Lose His Luck](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-merchant-who-tried-to-lose-his-luck/): You can’t throw away luck that is yours to keep.
- [Seven Good Years](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/seven-good-years/): Spend the good years well, and they may stay.
- [Elijah the Builder](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/elijah-the-builder/): Help sometimes knocks dressed as a beggar.
- [The Youngest Son’s Ten Friends](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-youngest-sons-ten-friends/): Look after your friends, and they will look after you.
- [The Grateful Dead](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-grateful-dead/): Pay a stranger’s debt, and it may pay you back.
- [The Language of the Ravens](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-jewish-world/the-language-of-the-ravens/): Throw out the messenger, and the message still arrives.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of West Africa (coming soon)

- [How the Stories Came to Anansi](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/how-the-stories-came-to-anansi/): Flattery is a rope. Vain creatures tie themselves up.
- [Anansi and the Pot of Wisdom](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/anansi-and-the-pot-of-wisdom/): No one head can hold all the world’s wisdom.
- [Thunder’s Pot and Thunder’s Stick](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/thunders-pot-and-thunders-stick/): Hide the pot from your children, and the stick will find you.
- [The Farm with No Road](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-farm-with-no-road/): What you take by a trick, a trick will take from you.
- [The Blind Fisherman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-blind-fisherman/): Sneer at the hands that guide you, and they’ll let go.
- [Anansi’s Hat of Hot Beans](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/anansis-hat-of-hot-beans/): Pretend you aren’t hungry, and the beans will tell on you.
- [The Nodding Image](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-nodding-image/): Steal from your own son, and you’ll eat at his table.
- [The Spider Who Borrowed Wings](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-spider-who-borrowed-wings/): Eat everyone’s share, and you’ll walk home alone.
- [Anansi Goes Looking for a Fool](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/anansi-goes-looking-for-a-fool/): Go looking for a fool, and you may find a mirror.
- [The Thing in the Spider’s Trap](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-thing-in-the-spiders-trap/): Rob a friend’s trap, and his trouble moves into your house.
- [The Monkey Who Called Names](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-monkey-who-called-names/): Say no if you must, but don’t call names.
- [Anansi and the Rubber Man](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/anansi-and-the-rubber-man/): Steal from your own family, and you’ll hide from them for ever.
- [The Stone That Ground by Itself](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-stone-that-ground-by-itself/): Take more than you need, and it will sit on you.
- [The Spotted Thing on the Anthill](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-spotted-thing-on-the-anthill/): Grab a partner’s share, and you’ll pay it back, piece by piece.
- [The Worm Who Lent His Eyes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-worm-who-lent-his-eyes/): Lend your eyes to the mighty, and you’ll walk blind.
- [Tortoise in the Drummer’s Sack](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/tortoise-in-the-drummers-sack/): Ride in another’s sack, and you’ll be beaten like a drum.
- [The Tree Where Nobody Talked](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-tree-where-nobody-talked/): When silence keeps you alive, don’t chatter about your luck.
- [The Hyena and the Three Feathers](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-hyena-and-the-three-feathers/): A coward will starve himself behind three feathers.
- [The Bat Who Ate the Lamb’s Dinner](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-bat-who-ate-the-lambs-dinner/): Eat your porter’s dinner, and you’ll eat alone in the dark.
- [Turtle Rides the Leopard](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/turtle-rides-the-leopard/): Make a fool of the leopard, and you’ll carry his marks.
- [The Tortoise Who Could Not Cry](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-tortoise-who-could-not-cry/): Hire someone to weep for you, and he’ll weep about you.
- [The Hippo Nobody Could Name](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-hippo-nobody-could-name/): Make your guests guess for their dinner, and you’ll lose your house.
- [Klo and the Palm Wine](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/klo-and-the-palm-wine/): Drink the master’s wine on the road, and you’ll crawl home.
- [The Hyena Who Wrestled the Lizard](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-hyena-who-wrestled-the-lizard/): Laugh at someone small, and you may run from him for ever.
- [Tortoise and the Cloud](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/tortoise-and-the-cloud/): Cheat a partner who brings the rain, and you’ll drown.
- [The Hunter and the Singing Tortoise](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-hunter-and-the-singing-tortoise/): A secret given to you is not yours to show off.
- [Ole and the Ants](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/ole-and-the-ants/): Watch your neighbours’ business, and the ants will eat yours.
- [Watch-Pot and Greedy](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/watch-pot-and-greedy/): The greedy man would rather be buried than share his rice.
- [Remember the River Yom](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/remember-the-river-yom/): Win all you like, but mind the river you must cross home.
- [Adzanumee, the Yam Daughter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/adzanumee-the-yam-daughter/): One cruel word can undo the thing you wished for most.
- [The Parrot Who Said “She Lies”](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-parrot-who-said-she-lies/): A liar can silence the truth-teller, but not the truth.
- [The Three Gluttons](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-three-gluttons/): Greed can’t wait for anything, not even to stay alive.
- [Ntyi and the Boa](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/ntyi-and-the-boa/): What one person can’t do alone, many friends can do together.
- [The Man Who Told All His Secrets](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-man-who-told-all-his-secrets/): Never tell a stranger the last trick you know.
- [Wait for Me, Big Sister](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/wait-for-me-big-sister/): Don’t leave the little one behind; you may need his kindness someday.
- [I Will Die God’s Death](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/i-will-die-gods-death/): No king can hurry a death that is not his to give.
- [The Leopard-Man](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-leopard-man/): When a stranger warns you twice, believe him the first time.
- [The Ape’s Kindness](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-apes-kindness/): Shoot the hand that heals your child, and lose your town.
- [The Hunter Who Became a Python](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/the-hunter-who-became-a-python/): Temper can kick over what it can never put back.
- [Abena Who Never Went Home](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-west-africa/abena-who-never-went-home/): Stay away too long, and home will not wait for you.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Central Africa (coming soon)

- [The Sparrow’s Tug-of-War](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-sparrows-tug-of-war/): Laugh at the small, and you’ll pull against yourself all day.
- [The Leopard Who Bowed to the Goat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-leopard-who-bowed-to-the-goat/): A long beard is not a strong jaw.
- [The Leopard’s Wine-Booth](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-leopards-wine-booth/): A tyrant’s law can be dodged, but never trusted.
- [The Leopard Who Played Dead](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-leopard-who-played-dead/): A dead man doesn’t flinch. Test him before you mourn.
- [Hare’s Long Basket](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/hares-long-basket/): Never climb into a basket your enemy wove.
- [The Turtle Who Feared the Water](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-turtle-who-feared-the-water/): Ask your enemy what he fears, and he will lie.
- [The Bird Who Copied the Owl](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-bird-who-copied-the-owl/): Copy a trick you don’t understand, and it cooks you.
- [The Path That Was Caught](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-path-that-was-caught/): Keep the shared path for yourself, and soon there’s no path.
- [The Turtle’s Greedy Trap](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-turtles-greedy-trap/): Gloat over a trapped beast, and lean too close.
- [The Ants Who Waited](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-ants-who-waited/): Patience gets the prize that biting loses.
- [The Elephant’s Son and the Crooked Guardian](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-elephants-son-and-the-crooked-guardian/): Cheat the child left in your care, and his father comes home.
- [The Leopard in the Goat’s Belly](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-leopard-in-the-goats-belly/): Hide inside your crime, and it becomes your grave.
- [The Leopard Who Wanted the Gazelle’s Wife](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-leopard-who-wanted-the-gazelles-wife/): Covet another man’s wife, and you’ll give away your claws.
- [Hog and His Cousin Boar](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/hog-and-his-cousin-boar/): Eat from another man’s pot, and one day you’ll be in it.
- [The Chicken Who Forgot the Fire](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-chicken-who-forgot-the-fire/): A messenger who stays for supper never delivers the message.
- [The Dog Who Came In from the Cold](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-dog-who-came-in-from-the-cold/): Knock and offer to help. The thief stays out in the cold.
- [The Water-Snake Who Went Fishing](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-water-snake-who-went-fishing/): Skip your mother’s call, and miss your share.
- [The Plantain-Eater’s Nest](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-plantain-eaters-nest/): Promise in the rain, forget in the sun, stay wet forever.
- [The Toad Who Invited the Ants](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-toad-who-invited-the-ants/): When a guest says his children eat everything, believe him.
- [The Palm-Rat Who Was Deaf When Eating](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-palm-rat-who-was-deaf-when-eating/): Be deaf to a friend, and he’ll be deaf to you.
- [Which Is the Fattest?](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/which-is-the-fattest/): Accept no test you know you cannot pass.
- [Dog and the Kingship](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/dog-and-the-kingship/): Grab the meat at your crowning, and lose the crown.
- [Cock and Fox](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/cock-and-fox/): Never tell your enemy your weapon is only for show.
- [Fox and Mole](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/fox-and-mole/): A thief’s secret tunnel leads to his own trap.
- [Partridge and Turtle](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/partridge-and-turtle/): Boast that you’ll escape, and the fire hears you.
- [The King of the Hogs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-king-of-the-hogs/): You eat in peace because someone else stays awake.
- [“It Is Mine!”](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/it-is-mine/): Claim everything, and you’ll own the trouble too.
- [The Blacksmith and the Blackbirds](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-blacksmith-and-the-blackbirds/): A debt denied by a flock is paid by every bird.
- [The Billy-Goat Lawsuit](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-billy-goat-lawsuit/): A male doesn’t give birth, and a cheat doesn’t win.
- [Who Cried All Night](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/who-cried-all-night/): A lie cries for an hour; the truth cries all night.
- [The Cassava Thieves](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-cassava-thieves/): Lift a thief’s load, and you carry his sentence.
- [How Kengi Lost Her Child](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/how-kengi-lost-her-child/): The rule you make for others will be used on you.
- [The Imp’s Bargain](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-imps-bargain/): Never laugh at a bargain until you’ve read all of it.
- [The Son Who Hid from His Father](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-son-who-hid-from-his-father/): You can’t hide from the one who raised you.
- [Come Closer, Said the Crocodile](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/come-closer-said-the-crocodile/): When someone keeps saying “Come closer,” step back.
- [The Singing Dogs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-singing-dogs/): Bury your crime, and the dogs will dig it up.
- [The Cloud-Wife’s Basket](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-cloud-wifes-basket/): Keep the one promise she asked, or lose all she gave.
- [The Fish-Wife](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-fish-wife/): Throw someone’s beginnings in her face, and she’ll go back to them.
- [The Spider Who Refused Every Suitor](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-spider-who-refused-every-suitor/): Refuse every honest offer, and a liar’s will look fine.
- [The Little Sister and the Ma-kishi](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-central-africa/the-little-sister-and-the-ma-kishi/): The little one you beat may be the one awake.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of East Africa and the Horn (coming soon)

- [The Gazelle Who Made a Sultan](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-gazelle-who-made-a-sultan/): Forget who lifted you, and you will wake where you began.
- [The Donkey Who Came Back](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-donkey-who-came-back/): Be fooled once, it’s bad luck. Twice, it’s your own doing.
- [The Father’s Blessing](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-fathers-blessing/): Grab the cattle and leave the blessing, and the cattle wander off.
- [Ha! and Hi!](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/ha-and-hi/): Trap an honest worker, and you’ll put your own finger in.
- [Goso the Teacher](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/goso-the-teacher/): Steal one fruit, and the whole world comes looking for you.
- [The Hare Who Was Thinking](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-hare-who-was-thinking/): Never agree to a rule you haven’t thought all the way through.
- [The Copper Needle](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-copper-needle/): Whoever pays you to betray, will not pay you after.
- [The Little Eel Who Played Dead](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-little-eel-who-played-dead/): A trick that works twice is not a trick that works forever.
- [The Crocodile and the Pig](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-crocodile-and-the-pig/): When a friend warns you about the bait, believe him.
- [Fine Clothes and Rough Cloth](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/fine-clothes-and-rough-cloth/): Fine clothes never dug a field. Helping hands did.
- [The Cat Who Broke the Oath](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-cat-who-broke-the-oath/): Break faith with one friend, and every friend stops trusting you.
- [The Wild Ox at the Spring](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-wild-ox-at-the-spring/): What you’re proudest of may be what catches you.
- [The Two Thieves and the Old Woman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-two-thieves-and-the-old-woman/): Wait. Wicked partners always end up eating each other.
- [The Hare Who Pretended to Dig](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-hare-who-pretended-to-dig/): Pretend to work, and the harvest will tell on you.
- [The Hyenas’ New Prophet](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-hyenas-new-prophet/): A prophet who tells you only good news is no prophet.
- [The Elephant Who Let the First Calf Go](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-elephant-who-let-the-first-calf-go/): Let a thief take one calf, and he’ll come for the cow.
- [Don’t Look Back](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/dont-look-back/): When your father says no, don’t sneak off and do it anyway.
- [Who Is in the Hare’s House?](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/who-is-in-the-hares-house/): A big voice can come out of a very small body.
- [The Coward and the Monkey](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-coward-and-the-monkey/): One coward’s shortcut can sink a whole company.
- [What Made Mawenzi Jagged](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/what-made-mawenzi-jagged/): Ask once for what you need. Ask again for treats, and see.
- [The Banana-Leaf Bundles](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-banana-leaf-bundles/): Give the poor man a fair share. He keeps the leaves.
- [After the Harvest, Carve Your Spoons](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/after-the-harvest-carve-your-spoons/): Bring in the harvest first. Carve the spoons after.
- [The Bird with the Broken Leg](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-bird-with-the-broken-leg/): Hurt something small, and something small will come back for you.
- [The Hyenas Who Flew for Fat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-hyenas-who-flew-for-fat/): Greed will climb any height, and fall from every one.
- [The Hyena Who Was Trusted](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-hyena-who-was-trusted/): Eat what you were trusted to guard, and the whole herd comes.
- [Kasanke, the Little Red Bird](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/kasanke-the-little-red-bird/): The loudest promises often run first.
- [The Foolish Hare](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-foolish-hare/): In the forest, somebody is always watching.
- [The Pot, the Drum and the Monkey](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-pot-the-drum-and-the-monkey/): Let a mischief-maker judge your quarrel, and you both lose.
- [Walukaga the Blacksmith](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/walukaga-the-blacksmith/): Ask for the impossible, and you may be asked it back.
- [Why the Bat Hides from the Sun](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/why-the-bat-hides-from-the-sun/): When you’re sent on an errand, go straight there.
- [The Axe of Clay](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-axe-of-clay/): Before you pay, ask what the axe is made of.
- [The Leopard Who Blamed the Goats](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-leopard-who-blamed-the-goats/): Don’t punish the small for what the big one did.
- [The Two Travellers](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-two-travellers/): Plan harm for your neighbour, and harm finds you first.
- [The Donkey Who Had to Bray](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-donkey-who-had-to-bray/): One loud mouth can bring the leopard to everyone.
- [The Boar Who Took Advice](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-boar-who-took-advice/): Advice is cheap when someone else pays for it.
- [The Hyena Who Lost His Herd](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-hyena-who-lost-his-herd/): Sleep through your own business, and someone else will run it.
- [When the Leopard Grows Old](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/when-the-leopard-grows-old/): Bully while you’re strong, and the weak will laugh later.
- [The Slap on the Hyena’s Cheek](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-slap-on-the-hyenas-cheek/): Learn from the slap on someone else’s cheek.
- [The Pot That Ate the Mutton](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-pot-that-ate-the-mutton/): A thief will carry the proof home on his own head.
- [The Vizier’s Letter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-east-africa-and-the-horn/the-viziers-letter/): Dig a pit for someone else, and you’ll fall in it.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Southern Africa (coming soon)

- [The Lion Who Would Not Listen to His Mother](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-lion-who-would-not-listen-to-his-mother/): Your mother has met the hunter. You have not.
- [The Lion Who Could Fly](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-lion-who-could-fly/): A bully’s wings rest on bones he cannot guard.
- [The Two-Headed Python](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-two-headed-python/): Order your echo killed, and you order your own end.
- [The Lion and the Baboon](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-lion-and-the-baboon/): Leap at the one who is watching, and meet the drop.
- [The Leopard and the Ram](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-leopard-and-the-ram/): Big talk at the right moment beats big teeth.
- [The Dove, the Heron and the Jackal](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-dove-the-heron-and-the-jackal/): Never show a bully how you guard yourself.
- [The Hyena Who Played Dead](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-hyena-who-played-dead/): Copy a trick without the wits, and you get the stick.
- [The Lazy Woman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-lazy-woman/): Laugh at the diggers, and you’ll end up in their pit.
- [The Tortoise and the Baboons](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-tortoise-and-the-baboons/): Serve your guest where he can’t reach, and expect the same.
- [The Giraffe and the Tortoise](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-giraffe-and-the-tortoise/): Swallow every small thing, and one will stick.
- [The Zebra Stallion](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-zebra-stallion/): Bully the mothers, and you’ll meet the son.
- [The Jackal Who Would Not Dig](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-jackal-who-would-not-dig/): A sweet tongue loses to a shut mouth.
- [The Elephant Who Ate the Beans](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-elephant-who-ate-the-beans/): Steal a friend’s supper in disguise, and he’ll make a better bow.
- [Lion and Little Jackal](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/lion-and-little-jackal/): Make a cheat’s bargain, and climb a mouse-skin rope.
- [Isuro and Gudu](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/isuro-and-gudu/): Teach a friend to cheat, and he’ll cheat you better.
- [Five Heads](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/five-heads/): Be rude to the little ones, and the big one hears.
- [Untombinde and the River Monster](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/untombinde-and-the-river-monster/): “Nothing comes back from there.” Believe it the first time.
- [Unanana and the One-Tusked Elephant](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/unanana-and-the-one-tusked-elephant/): Build in the road, and the road comes to your door.
- [Dance Like That!](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/dance-like-that/): When a new friend leads you away from home, turn back.
- [Demane and Demazana](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/demane-and-demazana/): Cook what you were told not to, and the hill smells it.
- [The Wonderful Feather](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-wonderful-feather/): Run from a broken pot, and you run toward worse.
- [The Disobedient Boy and the Big Snake](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-disobedient-boy-and-the-big-snake/): Don’t follow snake tracks, and don’t hit the one who warns you.
- [Kenkebe](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/kenkebe/): Eat alone in a famine, and you’ll face the dark alone.
- [The Bird That Made Milk](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-bird-that-made-milk/): Show off the thing that feeds you, and it flies.
- [Kgolodikane](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/kgolodikane/): Laugh at someone’s hurt, and the hurt hands you over.
- [The Little Wise Woman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-little-wise-woman/): When the smallest one reads the tracks, read them too.
- [The Rock with Eyes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-rock-with-eyes/): When the smallest says the rock has eyes, look.
- [The Hyrax Who Sent for His Tail](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-hyrax-who-sent-for-his-tail/): Nobody fetches your share for you. Go and get it.
- [The Hyena and the Moon](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-hyena-and-the-moon/): Drop what you hold for a shine, and lose both.
- [The Baboons and the Leopard](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-baboons-and-the-leopard/): When old enemies stroke your fur, count their sticks.
- [Uthlakanyana and the Iguana’s Whistle](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/uthlakanyana-and-the-iguanas-whistle/): The cleverest lender still lends to someone faster.
- [The Man Who Threw Away His Bread](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-man-who-threw-away-his-bread/): Throw away bread when you’re full; hunger remembers where.
- [Be-Thankful, the Dog Who Went Home](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/be-thankful-the-dog-who-went-home/): Feed the hunter on a broken pot, and he walks home.
- [The Wife Carved from Wood](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-wife-carved-from-wood/): Take what someone made with love, and hold a log.
- [The Wonderful Horns](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-wonderful-horns/): Turn away the ragged boy, and lose what he carries.
- [Simbukumbukwana](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/simbukumbukwana/): Leave the small one in the road, and you’ll need his roof.
- [The Boy with the Moon on His Chest](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-boy-with-the-moon-on-his-chest/): What jealousy hides grows up and walks home.
- [The Tortoise Nobody Ate](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/the-tortoise-nobody-ate/): A lie can carry you far, but not over water.
- [Seetetelane and the Ostrich-Egg Wife](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/seetetelane-and-the-ostrich-egg-wife/): One careless sentence can undo a whole life.
- [Masilo and Masilonyane](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southern-africa/masilo-and-masilonyane/): What you bury, a bird will sing.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Egypt and North Africa (coming soon)

- [The Eloquent Peasant](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-eloquent-peasant/): Bully the patient man, and his patience will outlast you.
- [The Shipwrecked Sailor](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-shipwrecked-sailor/): Hold your nerve; the worst wreck can wash you home.
- [The Magician Who Said “Not a Man”](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-magician-who-said-not-a-man/): Some wonders should not be worked, even for a king.
- [The Two Hundred Baskets](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-two-hundred-baskets/): Count what comes through your gate before you shut it.
- [The Book in the Tomb](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-book-in-the-tomb/): Steal from the dead, and you’ll carry it back in shame.
- [Setna and His Son](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/setna-and-his-son/): The scales weigh what you did, not what you wore.
- [The Lion and the Mouse](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-lion-and-the-mouse/): Don’t laugh at a small creature’s promise.
- [The Prince Who Had Three Fates](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-prince-who-had-three-fates/): Watch over the people you love; care beats bad luck.
- [The Man Who Ran Away](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-man-who-ran-away/): Run from a danger that isn’t there, and you’ll run for years.
- [The Prince Who Learned a Trade](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-prince-who-learned-a-trade/): A trade in your hands can buy back your life.
- [The Bravest Man in the Village](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-bravest-man-in-the-village/): Courage without sense goes in head first.
- [A Hundred Tricks and a Half](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/a-hundred-tricks-and-a-half/): One trick that works beats a hundred you brag about.
- [The Panther’s New Shoes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-panthers-new-shoes/): A guilty eye can’t help looking back.
- [The Jackal’s Seven Shares](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-jackals-seven-shares/): Weigh fairly; you never know who’s in the sack.
- [The Hedgehog in the Jar of Fat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-hedgehog-in-the-jar-of-fat/): Lean in for a secret, and you may lift out a hedgehog.
- [The Hyena Who Wanted to Eat Alone](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-hyena-who-wanted-to-eat-alone/): Grab someone else’s supper, and you’ll end up with none.
- [The Jackal Who Went to a Wedding](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-jackal-who-went-to-a-wedding/): A secret spoon in the shared jar gets found at the feast.
- [The Jackal Who Wanted Bright Eyes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-jackal-who-wanted-bright-eyes/): A dare that hurts you is a trick, not a beauty secret.
- [Man’s Head Is Black](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/mans-head-is-black/): Man’s head is black: help him, then keep your distance.
- [Climb, Then!](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/climb-then/): A threat that can’t climb is only noise.
- [The Falcon and the Old Owl](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-falcon-and-the-old-owl/): Pretend to be what you’re not, and your bragging will tell.
- [The Wren Who Measured the Camel](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-wren-who-measured-the-camel/): Spread your wings as wide as you like; the camel is bigger.
- [The Rooster Who Called the Imam](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-rooster-who-called-the-imam/): If someone wants you to come down, call your grown-up first.
- [The Hedgehog Who Rode a Hen](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-hedgehog-who-rode-a-hen/): Small doesn’t mean easy to swallow.
- [The Wagtail’s Witness](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-wagtails-witness/): A false witness pays first.
- [The Scorpion and the Farmhand](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-scorpion-and-the-farmhand/): Feed the hungry; you never know what kindness carries back.
- [The Soap-Seller’s Daughter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-soap-sellers-daughter/): Kindness plus cleverness beats a bully’s threats.
- [Ash for Flour](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/ash-for-flour/): A cheat always meets his twin at the market.
- [The Heap of Wheat and the River of Oil](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-heap-of-wheat-and-the-river-of-oil/): Boast of your heap, and someone will show you a river.
- [What Becomes of the Old Moons](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/what-becomes-of-the-old-moons/): Pretend to be a scholar, and you’ll get a scholar’s test.
- [The Serpent Before the King](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-serpent-before-the-king/): Before you cry for justice, tell who struck first.
- [The Bread the King Baked](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-bread-the-king-baked/): Do no harm, and no harm will come home to you.
- [The Riddling Traveller](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-riddling-traveller/): Before you call someone foolish, ask what their words mean.
- [Elias and the Breathing Haystack](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/elias-and-the-breathing-haystack/): Set a trap for a reader of tracks, and he’ll read it.
- [The Boy Who Lived with the Ostriches](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-boy-who-lived-with-the-ostriches/): Repay a kindness for as long as your people last.
- [The Sack of Ashes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-sack-of-ashes/): Empty a gift on the road, and you’ll arrive with dregs.
- [The Kadi Who Became a Heron](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-kadi-who-became-a-heron/): Laugh at people who fall, and you’ll be the next one down.
- [The Ghoula Eaten by the Jackals](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-ghoula-eaten-by-the-jackals/): Do good, and good will stand guard at your door.
- [Mqidech and the Ghoula](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/mqidech-and-the-ghoula/): Caught? Keep calm and keep thinking; wits open locked doors.
- [The Seven Sisters and the Ghoula](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-egypt-and-north-africa/the-seven-sisters-and-the-ghoula/): If your mother had no sister, don’t open to your aunt.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Arabia and the Nights (coming soon)

- [The Fisherman and the Jinni](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-fisherman-and-the-jinni/): Repay a kindness with harm, and back in the jar you go.
- [The Prince and the Ghoul](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-prince-and-the-ghoul/): Don’t ride off alone, and don’t follow a stranger inside.
- [The Dervish’s Ointment](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-dervishs-ointment/): One eye to see the treasure; greed wants the other.
- [The Black Stones on the Mountain](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-black-stones-on-the-mountain/): The voices behind you only win if you turn round.
- [The Jewels of the Brass City](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-jewels-of-the-brass-city/): When the owner says “leave it”, leave it.
- [Abu Kir and Abu Sir](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/abu-kir-and-abu-sir/): Carry your share for a friend, and never sell him out.
- [The Envier and the Envied](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-envier-and-the-envied/): Cheer when your neighbour does well; envy only shames the envier.
- [The Ebony Horse](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-ebony-horse/): Learn how to land before you learn to fly.
- [Ijbeyneh and the Ghoul’s Mountain](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/ijbeyneh-and-the-ghouls-mountain/): Never wander off alone, and never leave anyone behind.
- [The Camels’ Grievance](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-camels-grievance/): Ask a lot of others if you must, but never humiliate them.
- [The Treasure Under the Fountain](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-treasure-under-the-fountain/): Dig in your own garden before you cross the desert.
- [The Dog’s Dish of Gold](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-dogs-dish-of-gold/): Pay back what you owe, even if nobody would ever know.
- [Ali Cogia’s Olives](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/ali-cogias-olives/): Hide your theft in olives, and the olives tell the year.
- [The Barmecide’s Feast](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-barmecides-feast/): If you serve a joke, be ready to eat one.
- [The Donkey Who Was a Man](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-donkey-who-was-a-man/): The stranger the story, the harder you should check it.
- [Juha’s Peg](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/juhas-peg/): Before you shake hands on a deal, ask about every “except”.
- [The Little Hunchback](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-little-hunchback/): Hide a mistake, and it travels until it reaches the gallows.
- [The Drop of Honey](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-drop-of-honey/): Wipe up the drop before it becomes a war.
- [The City of Cheats](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-city-of-cheats/): Never promise “whatever you want”. A cheat will want everything.
- [The Bundle Too Cheap](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-bundle-too-cheap/): A bargain too good is somebody’s loss.
- [Abu Nuwas and the Judge Who Believed in Dreams](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/abu-nuwas-and-the-judge-who-believed-in-dreams/): A rule you make for others is a rule for you too.
- [Stretch Your Legs to Your Quilt](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/stretch-your-legs-to-your-quilt/): When the quilt is short, bend your knees.
- [The Old Man’s Figs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-old-mans-figs/): Bring a gift for gold, and you’ll get your gift back.
- [The Two Beggars and the Roast Fowl](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-two-beggars-and-the-roast-fowl/): Never sell a gift before you’ve looked inside it.
- [The Boaster and the Skulls](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-boaster-and-the-skulls/): Don’t boast about your grandfathers; show us who you are.
- [The Judge’s Sack of Earth](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-judges-sack-of-earth/): What you take unfairly weighs more than you can carry.
- [Jaafar and the Beanseller](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/jaafar-and-the-beanseller/): Never forget the one who helped you when you were cold.
- [The Wolf and the Fox](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-wolf-and-the-fox/): Hit the friend who warns you, and you’ll walk into the pit.
- [The Lion Cub and the Carpenter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-lion-cub-and-the-carpenter/): Climb into a box built by flattery, and it’s nailed shut.
- [The Woodseller’s Candles](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-woodsellers-candles/): Shut one door on an honest worker, and he finds two more.
- [The Mouse and the Weasel](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-mouse-and-the-weasel/): When the thief offers you a share, look for the stick.
- [Sa’id and Lulu](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/said-and-lulu/): Share fairly in easy times; you will need friends in hard ones.
- [Why the Dog Is Tied](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/why-the-dog-is-tied/): When you’re trusted with something precious, keep watch over it.
- [Hunayn’s Boots](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/hunayns-boots/): Chase a bargain far enough and lose the camel.
- [Hatim’s Horse](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/hatims-horse/): Share your best with a hungry guest, even when it hurts.
- [Hatim’s Guests](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/hatims-guests/): Don’t make fun of people, even when they can’t hear you.
- [The Goatherd’s Four Goats](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/the-goatherds-four-goats/): Be kind with what you have; don’t wait until you’re rich.
- [Daher and the Mare](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/daher-and-the-mare/): Cheat a kind man and you rob every beggar after you.
- [Ma’n and the Cucumber Man](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/man-and-the-cucumber-man/): Speak of others as if they’re listening. One day they will be.
- [Ahikar and the Ungrateful Nephew](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-arabia-and-the-nights/ahikar-and-the-ungrateful-nephew/): Repay the people who raised you with thanks, never with lies.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Persia, Anatolia and the Caucasus (coming soon)

- [The Elephant’s Wife](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-elephants-wife/): Run from a shared trouble, and it comes back doubled.
- [The Fox Who Wooed for the Miller](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-fox-who-wooed-for-the-miller/): Pretend to be a pasha, and you’ll have to face one.
- [The Fox and the Partridge](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-fox-and-the-partridge/): Swear falsely once, and nobody believes your groans.
- [The Cat Who Stole the Milk](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-cat-who-stole-the-milk/): A thief can pay it back, but can’t undo it.
- [Eat, My Coat!](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/eat-my-coat/): Welcome the person, not the coat.
- [The Grey Wolf and the Badger](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-grey-wolf-and-the-badger/): When a wolf promises a soft bed, ask what it’s made of.
- [The Fox, the Eagle and the Wolf](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-fox-the-eagle-and-the-wolf/): A cheat thinks every warning is a trick, and that sinks him.
- [The Bristle That Came Too Late](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-bristle-that-came-too-late/): Can’t swim? Stay out of the water, and shout for help fast.
- [The Peg in the Ruins](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-peg-in-the-ruins/): Say no to the midnight dare. In the dark, fear grabs hardest.
- [The Three Strays](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-three-strays/): Lost and small? Keep your head, and stay together till help comes.
- [Baldhead and the Scanty-Beards](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/baldhead-and-the-scanty-beards/): Greedy ears believe anything, even a river full of sheep.
- [The Swallow and the Mosquito](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-swallow-and-the-mosquito/): A true friend speaks up for you when you can’t.
- [The Rock of Wishes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-rock-of-wishes/): Hand your horse to a stranger, and you walk home.
- [The Man Who Went to Find His Luck](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-man-who-went-to-find-his-luck/): Luck won’t chase the man who keeps walking past it.
- [The Wolf-Aunt](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-wolf-aunt/): Wave off a warning at home, and the wolf moves in.
- [The Colt Who Lost His Wings](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-colt-who-lost-his-wings/): Wait the forty days; one peek can cost the wings.
- [The Maiden of the Sea](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-maiden-of-the-sea/): Keep a kindness going, and it comes back when you need it.
- [Three Brothers and the Div](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/three-brothers-and-the-div/): Keep your head and think; a quick wit beats a big bully.
- [The Language of Birds](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-language-of-birds/): Don’t pass your bad luck to someone else; it comes back.
- [The Fisherman’s Son](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-fishermans-son/): Spare the small creature today; tomorrow it may hide you.
- [The Sparrow’s Warning](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-sparrows-warning/): Be kind to the sparrow, and listen when it warns you.
- [Roads and Shortcuts](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/roads-and-shortcuts/): Shortcuts are only short until the bill arrives.
- [The Serpent and the Peasant](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-serpent-and-the-peasant/): A friend only in good times is no friend.
- [Shah Abbas and the Cobbler Faraj](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/shah-abbas-and-the-cobbler-faraj/): Lose one trade? Find another by supper, and keep singing.
- [The Thorn-Gatherer Who Left God’s Country](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-thorn-gatherer-who-left-gods-country/): Grumble at your daily bread, and you’ll pay dear for it.
- [The Sorcerer and His Pupil](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-sorcerer-and-his-pupil/): Keep learning, and no trap can hold you for long.
- [Mullah Bazid’s Second Coat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/mullah-bazids-second-coat/): Practise what you preach, or someone will practise it for you.
- [Jamshid’s Pride](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/jamshids-pride/): Forget who gave you your crown, and it forgets you.
- [Amirani in Chains](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/amirani-in-chains/): Turn your strength on the weak, and it becomes your chain.
- [A Wise Weaver](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/a-wise-weaver/): Wisdom isn’t handed out by rank. Ask the weaver.
- [The Flying Throne](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-flying-throne/): Don’t ride anything you can’t steer or stop.
- [The Forty Lies](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-forty-lies/): A promise made before everyone must be kept, even by a khan.
- [The Talking Door](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-talking-door/): Do wrong, and your own eyes give you away.
- [The Virgin Queen](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-virgin-queen/): Wish the old man well, and he’ll tell you the way.
- [Rustam and the Div Akvan](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/rustam-and-the-div-akvan/): If you always do the opposite, you’re easy to steer.
- [The Cadi and the Jewel Bag](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-cadi-and-the-jewel-bag/): Greed drops what it holds to grab what glitters.
- [The Three Precepts](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/the-three-precepts/): Advice you paid for is worthless if you ignore it.
- [Shah Abbas and the Ring](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/shah-abbas-and-the-ring/): Never call someone a thief until you’ve asked what happened.
- [Selling the Wind](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/selling-the-wind/): Refuse a fair wage, and see who sells you the wind.
- [Salman and Rostom](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-persia-anatolia-and-the-caucasus/salman-and-rostom/): Two who will never give way shake the whole world.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of India (coming soon)

- [The Monkey and the Wedge](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-monkey-and-the-wedge/): Leave alone the work you do not understand.
- [The Crane and the Crab](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-crane-and-the-crab/): Who carries you for free means to eat you.
- [The Crow and the Golden Chain](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-crow-and-the-golden-chain/): When claws fail, use your head.
- [The Lion and the Clever Hare](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-lion-and-the-clever-hare/): Pride will fight its own reflection.
- [The Blue Jackal](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-blue-jackal/): Whoever forgets his own people will betray himself.
- [The Camel Who Offered Himself](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-camel-who-offered-himself/): When flatterers offer, they never mean it.
- [The Talkative Tortoise](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-talkative-tortoise/): A shut mouth keeps you in the air.
- [The Three Fishes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-three-fishes/): When the warning comes, swim.
- [Right-Mind and Wrong-Mind](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/right-mind-and-wrong-mind/): A lie needs a hiding place, and smoke finds it.
- [The Foolish Friend](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-foolish-friend/): Better a wise enemy than a foolish friend.
- [How the Birds Chose a King](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/how-the-birds-chose-a-king/): One sneer can make an enemy for life.
- [The Frogs Who Rode the Snake](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-frogs-who-rode-the-snake/): When your enemy offers a ride, count your friends.
- [The Crows and the Owls](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-crows-and-the-owls/): Never trust an enemy who comes to you for shelter.
- [The Crow and the Egret](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-crow-and-the-egret/): A bribe can buy a verdict, but not the truth.
- [How the Old Man’s Sons Were Duped](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/how-the-old-mans-sons-were-duped/): Love that waits for the money bag is not love.
- [The Ungrateful Goat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-ungrateful-goat/): Scorn the hand that fed you, and no hand will.
- [The Monkey and the Jackal](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-monkey-and-the-jackal/): Throw your friend the peel, and he will remember it.
- [The Loyal Mongoose](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-loyal-mongoose/): Look twice before you strike once.
- [The Lion-Makers](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-lion-makers/): Learning without sense will get you eaten.
- [The Weaver-Birds and the Monkeys](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-weaver-birds-and-the-monkeys/): Don’t give advice to those who didn’t ask for it.
- [The Jackal, the Goat and the Wolf Who Judged](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-jackal-the-goat-and-the-wolf-who-judged/): A judge your enemy chooses has already chosen.
- [The Mouse Who Became a Tiger](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-mouse-who-became-a-tiger/): Raise up the ungrateful and they bite the hand.
- [The Three Rogues and the Goat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-three-rogues-and-the-goat/): Say a lie three times and a fool believes it.
- [The Quarrel of the Quails](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-quarrel-of-the-quails/): Pull together or be bagged together.
- [The Selfish Sparrow and the Houseless Crows](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-selfish-sparrow-and-the-houseless-crows/): Shut the door on neighbours and they help themselves.
- [The Merchant of Seri](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-merchant-of-seri/): Cheat the poor tomorrow and lose the gold today.
- [The Deer Who Skipped His Lessons](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-deer-who-skipped-his-lessons/): Skip your lessons and the snare will teach you.
- [The Banyan Deer](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-banyan-deer/): A true leader steps in front of his weakest.
- [The Goblin’s Riddle: The Poisoned Rice](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-goblins-riddle-the-poisoned-rice/): Blame no one for an accident, or the blame sticks to you.
- [The Ghost Who Was Afraid of Being Bagged](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-ghost-who-was-afraid-of-being-bagged/): A cool head can bag a ghost.
- [The Tiger, the Brahmin and the Jackal](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-tiger-the-brahmin-and-the-jackal/): Before you open a cage, ask who’s inside.
- [Mighty-of-Mouth and Mighty-of-Hands](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/mighty-of-mouth-and-mighty-of-hands/): Strong hands win fights, but a quick tongue wins nights.
- [The Robbers Who Made Them Dance](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-robbers-who-made-them-dance/): Gloat over the beaten, and you will be beaten.
- [Tit for Tat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/tit-for-tat/): Play a trick on your ride, and remember the river home.
- [The Ghost Who Stole a House](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-ghost-who-stole-a-house/): A boaster will climb into any bottle you hold.
- [The Close Alliance](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-close-alliance/): Don’t tie your tail to a coward’s.
- [The Demon and the Curly Hair](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-demon-and-the-curly-hair/): Help that costs nothing can cost you everything.
- [The Jackal and the Iguana](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-jackal-and-the-iguana/): Make others praise you, and they’ll make up their own song.
- [The Beggar and the Five Pancakes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-beggar-and-the-five-pancakes/): Lose a whole life to win one pancake.
- [The King Who Would Not Bow](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-india/the-king-who-would-not-bow/): When a stranger asks you to kneel, ask him to go first.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of China (coming soon)

- [The Snipe and the Clam](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-snipe-and-the-clam/): Two who won’t let go make a third man’s supper.
- [The Fox Who Walked in Front of the Tiger](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-fox-who-walked-in-front-of-the-tiger/): Before you fear the fox, look at who walks behind him.
- [Drawing Legs on the Snake](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/drawing-legs-on-the-snake/): Finish, then stop. The extra leg costs the cup.
- [Two Farmers of Song: the Stump and the Sprouts](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/two-farmers-of-song-the-stump-and-the-sprouts/): Luck won’t come twice, and millet won’t hurry.
- [The Frog in the Well](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-frog-in-the-well/): Your well is not the world.
- [Learning to Walk in Handan](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/learning-to-walk-in-handan/): Copy someone else’s walk, and you’ll crawl home.
- [Two Fools of the Market: the Spear and Shield, and the Measuring String](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/two-fools-of-the-market-the-spear-and-shield-and-the-measuring-string/): Don’t boast both ways, and trust your own two feet.
- [Mr. Nanguo Plays the Pipes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/mr-nanguo-plays-the-pipes/): Hide in the crowd, and one day the crowd goes home.
- [The Fierce Dog and the Sour Wine](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-fierce-dog-and-the-sour-wine/): A snarling gate keeps out friends as well as thieves.
- [North to Reach the South](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/north-to-reach-the-south/): A fast horse only gets you lost faster.
- [The Man Who Loved Seagulls](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-man-who-loved-seagulls/): Come as a friend with a trap, and lose the friend.
- [Rich Mr. Guo and Poor Mr. Xiang](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/rich-mr-guo-and-poor-mr-xiang/): Ask what the trick means before you copy it.
- [The Monkey Who Caught Arrows](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-monkey-who-caught-arrows/): Show off to the archer, and he brings his friends.
- [The Marquis Who Loved a Seabird](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-marquis-who-loved-a-seabird/): Love it the way it needs, not the way you like.
- [The Mantis, the Cicada and the Oriole](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-mantis-the-cicada-and-the-oriole/): Watch your back while you watch your dinner.
- [Hundun and the Seven Holes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/hundun-and-the-seven-holes/): Some kindness is only a chisel in disguise.
- [The Duke Who Was Not Ill](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-duke-who-was-not-ill/): Laugh at the doctor, and the sickness has the last laugh.
- [The Ten Straw Hats](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-ten-straw-hats/): Throw out the good man, and you throw out your roof.
- [The Roc and the Island of Gold](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-roc-and-the-island-of-gold/): Take what you can carry, and leave before sunrise.
- [The Magic Cask](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-magic-cask/): Scold the old for being slow, and your luck leaves with them.
- [False Economy](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/false-economy/): Pinch the wrong penny, and you freeze under an empty quilt.
- [The Moon-Cake](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-moon-cake/): If someone offers to improve your cake, keep your cake.
- [Stolen Garlic](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/stolen-garlic/): A thief can hide the garlic, but not where he sold it.
- [The Miser and the Tiger](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-miser-and-the-tiger/): Love money more than life, and you keep neither.
- [Ximen Bao and the River God’s Bride](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/ximen-bao-and-the-river-gods-bride/): Those who sell others to the river should go first.
- [Zhou Chu and the Three Evils](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/zhou-chu-and-the-three-evils/): If the village cheers when you vanish, change before you return.
- [Kuafu Chases the Sun](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/kuafu-chases-the-sun/): Measure your strength before you race the sun.
- [The Monkey in the Buddha’s Hand](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-monkey-in-the-buddhas-hand/): Boast you can leap the world, and land in a bigger hand.
- [Lord Ye Who Loved Dragons](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/lord-ye-who-loved-dragons/): Love the picture all you like. The real thing has teeth.
- [Planting a Pear-Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/planting-a-pear-tree/): Refuse one pear, and you feed the whole market.
- [The Daoist of Mount Lao](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-daoist-of-mount-lao/): Skip the chores, and the wall will teach you.
- [The Theft of a Duck](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-theft-of-a-duck/): Steal a duck, and it grows its feathers on you.
- [The Great Rat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-great-rat/): The one who rushes first tires first.
- [The Tiger of Zhaocheng](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-tiger-of-zhaocheng/): Take a mother’s son, and you must become her son.
- [Friendship with Foxes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/friendship-with-foxes/): Ride with a thief, and be dropped far from home.
- [Fox-Fire](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/fox-fire/): What you steal is only borrowed.
- [The Ghost Who Was Sold as a Goat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-ghost-who-was-sold-as-a-goat/): Tell a stranger your weakness, and be sold by sundown.
- [The Weiqi Ghost](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-weiqi-ghost/): A game that eats your duties will eat you too.
- [The Coffin by the River](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-coffin-by-the-river/): Break a coffin for treasure, and the owner may object.
- [The Ant on the Reed](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-china/the-ant-on-the-reed/): Save the smallest life you can, and it may save yours.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Japan (coming soon)

- [The Tongue-Cut Sparrow](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-tongue-cut-sparrow/): Greed always picks the heavy basket.
- [The Ash That Made the Trees Bloom](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-ash-that-made-the-trees-bloom/): Copy a kind man’s luck, not his kindness, and lose both.
- [The Old Man’s Lump](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-old-mans-lump/): Dance for joy, not for profit; the audience can tell.
- [The Fountain of Youth](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-fountain-of-youth/): Take one cup of a good thing, never the whole spring.
- [The Price of a Smell](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-price-of-a-smell/): Sell a smell, and you’ll be paid in sounds.
- [The Moon Princess’s Impossible Gifts](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-moon-princesss-impossible-gifts/): A lie made of gold still sends its bill.
- [Benkei’s Thousandth Sword](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/benkeis-thousandth-sword/): Collect enough victories, and you’ll meet the one who collects you.
- [The Last Arrow](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-last-arrow/): When two arrows fail, think before the third.
- [Urashima Taro](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/urashima-taro/): Some boxes are kept shut by promises, not locks.
- [The Shark-Man’s Tears](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-shark-mans-tears/): A stranger you shelter may weep you a fortune.
- [The Three Potted Trees](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-three-potted-trees/): What you burn for a guest, the guest remembers.
- [The Waterfall of Yoro](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-waterfall-of-yoro/): The spring rewards the dutiful, not the thirsty.
- [The Man Who Wanted Forever](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-man-who-wanted-forever/): Wish for forever, and you’ll beg for an ending.
- [The Old Woman and the Rolling Dumpling](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-old-woman-and-the-rolling-dumpling/): Chase what you dropped, and you’ll cook for oni.
- [The Monkey and the Crab](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-monkey-and-the-crab/): Cheat the small, and the small will club together.
- [The Badger’s Money](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-badgers-money/): Give kindness freely, and repay it honestly.
- [The Fox Cub and the Old Tanuki](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-fox-cub-and-the-old-tanuki/): Bet against a trickster, and you’re the trick.
- [The Jellyfish and the Monkey](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-jellyfish-and-the-monkey/): Go with a stranger, and you’ll need your wits to get home.
- [The Lucky Tea-Kettle](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-lucky-tea-kettle/): Treat a strange thing kindly, and it may feed you.
- [The Man Who Laughed at Foxes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-man-who-laughed-at-foxes/): The surest man at the table is the easiest fooled.
- [The Hunter Who Trusted His Eyes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-hunter-who-trusted-his-eyes/): Ask why a wonder chose you before you kneel to it.
- [The Monkey Who Saved His Own Skin](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-monkey-who-saved-his-own-skin/): A servant’s worth is learned the day you’d sell him.
- [The Kappa’s Promise](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-kappas-promise/): Grab at something bigger than you, and it drags you home.
- [The Turban Shell](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-turban-shell/): Hide in your shell too long, and you’ll end up for sale.
- [The Two Frogs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-two-frogs/): Look with the back of your head, and every city is home.
- [The Firefly Princess](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-firefly-princess/): Who chases a bright thing ends in the lamp.
- [The Bee in the Web](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-bee-in-the-web/): Save one small life, and a million may come to help.
- [Chin-Chin Kobakama](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/chin-chin-kobakama/): Hide your mess, and it will dance for you at midnight.
- [The Face in the Well](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-face-in-the-well/): When deep water smiles up at you, step back.
- [Issun-boshi, the One-Inch Boy](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/issun-boshi-the-one-inch-boy/): You don’t have to be big to be brave.
- [The Boy Who Drew Cats](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-boy-who-drew-cats/): Keep to small places at night.
- [The Goblin Spider](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-goblin-spider/): Stay where the strange music can’t reach your hands.
- [The Ogre’s Arm](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-ogres-arm/): Show off your trophy, and its owner will come to fetch it.
- [The Hag of Adachigahara](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-hag-of-adachigahara/): When a host forbids one door, leave before dark.
- [Shippeitaro](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/shippeitaro/): Sing your secret loud enough, and someone will hear the name.
- [The Priest Who Dreamed He Was a Carp](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-priest-who-dreamed-he-was-a-carp/): However hungry you are, don’t bite what you were warned about.
- [The Hundred Ghosts](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-hundred-ghosts/): Ghost stories are for daylight; the dark makes them grow.
- [The Devil He Made Himself](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-devil-he-made-himself/): A guilty heart builds its own ghost.
- [The Wife He Left](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/the-wife-he-left/): Come back too late, and they’ll be waiting anyway.
- [Kwashin Koji’s Picture](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-japan/kwashin-kojis-picture/): What you take by force goes blank in your hands.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Korea (coming soon)

- [Heungbu and Nolbu](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/heungbu-and-nolbu/): What you break to get rich will break you back.
- [The Old Man in Plain Clothes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-old-man-in-plain-clothes/): Judge the man, not the coat he is wearing.
- [The Cat, the Dog and the Amber Bead](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-cat-the-dog-and-the-amber-bead/): Open your mouth to boast, and out drops the treasure.
- [The Sluggard’s Cure](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-sluggards-cure/): Let others carry your load, and the geese come to collect.
- [The Skull Under the Creeper](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-skull-under-the-creeper/): Kindness to the forgotten dead is never forgotten.
- [The Gold in the River](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-gold-in-the-river/): Throw away the gold that makes you hate your brother.
- [The Mirror from Seoul](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-mirror-from-seoul/): Before you shout at a stranger, check whose face it is.
- [The Friend Who Fed Your Family](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-friend-who-fed-your-family/): Before you curse your friend, ask who has been feeding you.
- [The Examination Riddle](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-examination-riddle/): What the king sees at night becomes the question by day.
- [The Student Who Stayed Behind](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-student-who-stayed-behind/): The one who keeps the watch is the one the king sees.
- [Ondal the Fool](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/ondal-the-fool/): Say it in fun, and you may have to mean it.
- [Half a Mirror](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/half-a-mirror/): Keep the promise, even when the other half comes late.
- [The Three Wise Sayings](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-three-wise-sayings/): Wisdom costs dear, but it is cheaper than a funeral.
- [The Tiger and the Dried Persimmon](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-tiger-and-the-dried-persimmon/): Fear a word you don’t know, and a thief will ride you.
- [The Rabbit and the Turtle](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-rabbit-and-the-turtle/): A flatterer’s back is a bad boat.
- [Bones for the Shad](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/bones-for-the-shad/): Be careful what you beg a king for.
- [The Tiger on the Ice](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-tiger-on-the-ice/): Greed shuts its eyes while the fire is laid.
- [Who Is the Eldest?](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/who-is-the-eldest/): The one who has read the most has lived the longest.
- [A Husband for Miss Mole](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/a-husband-for-miss-mole/): Pride walks around the world to find what was at home.
- [The Bear Who Fought the Stone](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-bear-who-fought-the-stone/): Rage at a stone, and the stone always wins.
- [Brother Tiger](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/brother-tiger/): Even a tiger who calls you mother keeps faith to the grave.
- [The Magpie Bridge](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-magpie-bridge/): Forget your work for love, and love comes once a year.
- [The Unmannerly Tiger](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-unmannerly-tiger/): Repay a rescue with teeth, and the rocks will judge you.
- [Mr Long Body and Miss Thousand Feet](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/mr-long-body-and-miss-thousand-feet/): Count the shoes before you count the wedding guests.
- [The Magpie’s New Coat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-magpies-new-coat/): Won’t stand still for the fitting? Then wear the ink forever.
- [The Fox Who Lost His Tail](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-fox-who-lost-his-tail/): Chase the slow too hard and you’ll leave your tail behind.
- [The Sun and the Moon](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-sun-and-the-moon/): Never open the door to a voice you don’t know.
- [The Story Bought for a Hundred Strings](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-story-bought-for-a-hundred-strings/): A foolish story, told every night, can scare a clever thief.
- [The Brave Magistrate](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-brave-magistrate/): The goblin eats the frightened first.
- [The Goblins’ Golden Club](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-goblins-golden-club/): Cheat your brother of seed, and reap a nose like an elephant’s.
- [The Horse That Knew the Way Home](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-horse-that-knew-the-way-home/): Every thief leaves something behind that knows the way home.
- [The Toad in the Dark Jar](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-toad-in-the-dark-jar/): A guilty finger stays dry, and a dry finger tells.
- [The King’s Letter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-kings-letter/): The king may write the letter; Heaven chooses who carries it.
- [The Man Who Bought a Title](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-man-who-bought-a-title/): Buy a fine name, and read what comes with it.
- [Chin and King Yama’s Messengers](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/chin-and-king-yamas-messengers/): Ask your enemy what he fears, and never tell him yours.
- [The Pheasant and the Bell](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-pheasant-and-the-bell/): A life you spare may one day ring for yours.
- [The Sparrows and the Flies](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-sparrows-and-the-flies/): Start a war you can’t finish, and you’ll hop forever.
- [The Woodcutter Who Watched the Game](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-woodcutter-who-watched-the-game/): Stop to watch the game, and the world goes on without you.
- [The Ragged Boy at the Feast](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-ragged-boy-at-the-feast/): Mock the stranger at your feast, and the feast is your last.
- [The Son Who Raised His Hand](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-korea/the-son-who-raised-his-hand/): The sky sees what happens behind the house walls.
