- [The Tiger’s Bargain](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-tigers-bargain/): A rule you agree to will bite you too.
- [The Sick Tiger King](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-sick-tiger-king/): Flatter a hungry king, and you may be the meal.
- [The Flower-Pecker’s Promise](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-flower-peckers-promise/): Believe a boast too big, and you lose what you held.
- [The Mouse-Deer and the Giant at the Fish Hut](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-mouse-deer-and-the-giant-at-the-fish-hut/): A thief who comes back nightly will meet someone waiting.
- [The Two Wild Bulls](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-two-wild-bulls/): Believe every tale-bearer, and you fight the wrong enemy.
- [The Tiger and the King’s Gong](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-tiger-and-the-kings-gong/): Never poke a thing because someone says it’s royal.
- [The Ape Who Asked to Be Stewed](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-ape-who-asked-to-be-stewed/): Copy a trick you don’t understand, and it isn’t the same trick.
- [The Monkey and the Turtle](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-monkey-and-the-turtle/): Greed climbs fastest and falls hardest.
- [The Hummingbird and the Carabao](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-hummingbird-and-the-carabao/): Never bet against the sea.
- [The Monkeys and the Dragonflies](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-monkeys-and-the-dragonflies/): Swing a club in a crowd and you hit your friends.
- [The Battle of the Crabs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-battle-of-the-crabs/): Pick a fight with the sea, and the sea wins.
- [The Greedy Crow](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-greedy-crow/): Chase what someone else has, and lose what you had.
- [The Monkey Who Traded Up](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-monkey-who-traded-up/): Trick your way up, and one bite brings you down.
- [The Dog Who Scratched in the Pig’s Place](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-dog-who-scratched-in-the-pigs-place/): Look at the work before you praise the worker.
- [The Elephant’s Bet](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-elephants-bet/): Bet your life to win an argument, and someone will collect.
- [The Four Paws of the Cat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-four-paws-of-the-cat/): Everyone whose leg ran with the fire pays for the fire.
- [The Man in the Mango Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-man-in-the-mango-tree/): Grab for the reward, and you may hang by it.
- [The Elephant’s Mouth](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-elephants-mouth/): Envy will put its hand in any mouth.
- [The False Fortune-Teller](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-false-fortune-teller/): A lucky lie needs another, and another, and then it costs.
- [The Clever Wife’s Riddle](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-clever-wifes-riddle/): Hear the whole riddle before you hand over the goods.
- [The Crow Is White](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-crow-is-white/): Agree at home, and the river fills your net.
- [The Donkey Who Walked with the Lion](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-donkey-who-walked-with-the-lion/): Walk beside a lion, and you are still a donkey.
- [Strife and Peace](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/strife-and-peace/): One quiet day was worth a hundred pieces of silver.
- [Poison-Mouth](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/poison-mouth/): Careless curses come true for somebody.
- [The Man with the Coconuts](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-man-with-the-coconuts/): Hurry with a heavy load, and you’ll be home by moonlight.
- [The Stone on Trial](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-stone-on-trial/): Pay to gawk, and your coins may feed somebody else.
- [Cuội and the Banyan Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/cu-i-and-the-banyan-tree/): Keep the one rule you were given.
- [The Grain of Rice](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-grain-of-rice/): Strike the gift, and the gift stops coming.
- [The Messenger Who Became a Dung Beetle](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-messenger-who-became-a-dung-beetle/): Carry the message exactly, or carry something worse.
- [Why the Buffalo Has No Upper Teeth](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/why-the-buffalo-has-no-upper-teeth/): Lend what you need, and you may never get it back.
- [The Masters Who Wanted to Be Young](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-masters-who-wanted-to-be-young/): Cruel hearts wanting young faces may get tails instead.
- [The Smith Who Wished to Be the Moon](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-smith-who-wished-to-be-the-moon/): Wish to be everything, and you’ll be stuck as one thing.
- [The Sao Bird Who Told the Truth](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-sao-bird-who-told-the-truth/): Tell the truth, and only about what you really saw.
- [The Dead Tiger’s Whiskers](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-dead-tigers-whiskers/): Do not kick a tiger, not even a dead one.
- [Lemon-Grass Crag](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/lemon-grass-crag/): Quarrel at a wedding, and you may stand there forever.
- [The Gedembai Who Called Your Name](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-gedembai-who-called-your-name/): Not every voice that calls your name deserves an answer.
- [The Alan’s Bead](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-alans-bead/): Grab for the last bead, and lose the whole house.
- [The Cow Who Wanted a Bath](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-cow-who-wanted-a-bath/): Stop for a bath mid-escape, and you’ll leave in the wrong skin.
- [The Hawk’s Lost Ring](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-hawks-lost-ring/): Break a promise, and you’ll scratch for it forever.
- [The First Monkey](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-southeast-asia/the-first-monkey/): Gamble away your chores, and you’ll swing in the trees.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of the Steppe and Siberia (coming soon)

- [The Letter from the Sky](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-letter-from-the-sky/): The road you build for an enemy, you will walk yourself.
- [The Three Brothers and the Lost Camel](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-three-brothers-and-the-lost-camel/): A thief’s own judgement is his best witness.
- [The Blind Man’s Claim](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-blind-mans-claim/): A lie talks loudest when it thinks it is alone.
- [The Khan’s Clever Daughter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-khans-clever-daughter/): Sneer at the poorest man, and he may sit on your throne.
- [The Khan’s Life-Stone](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-khans-life-stone/): A promise broken by a khan breaks the khan.
- [The Poor Man and His Luck](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-poor-man-and-his-luck/): Cheat, and your luck wears rags; hoard, and it leaves.
- [The Hunter Who Would Leave None](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-hunter-who-would-leave-none/): Take what you need, and leave the rest to grow.
- [The Golden Mountain](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-golden-mountain/): Leave a man on a mountain, and the mountain keeps you.
- [The Merchant’s Son](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-merchants-son/): Mistreat a workman, and one day he may be khan.
- [The Clay Jewel](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-clay-jewel/): Paid witnesses can’t shape a jewel they never saw.
- [The Bat Who Belonged to Nobody](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-bat-who-belonged-to-nobody/): Dodge every side’s dues, and no side will take you in.
- [The Corncrake’s Secret](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-corncrakes-secret/): Laugh at how someone walks, and he’ll keep what he knows.
- [The Prince’s Last Word](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-princes-last-word/): A secret crime still leaves a word behind.
- [Good and Evil on the Road](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/good-and-evil-on-the-road/): What you do to a companion waits for you on the road.
- [Zhirenshe the Wise](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/zhirenshe-the-wise/): Make impossible demands, and a clever answer will make you the fool.
- [The Fox and the Quail](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-fox-and-the-quail/): A cheat who trusts nobody still trusts the wrong bird.
- [The Old Man and the Forest Spirit](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-old-man-and-the-forest-spirit/): A bluff lasts as long as the other fellow’s fear.
- [The Hare’s Letter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-hares-letter/): A brave face can be worth a thousand teeth.
- [The Owl and the Rope of Sunlight](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-owl-and-the-rope-of-sunlight/): A head no bigger than a thumb can still outthink a giant.
- [The Hedgehog Judge](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-hedgehog-judge/): You don’t need long legs to stand up to a bully.
- [The Camel and the Deer](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-camel-and-the-deer/): What you borrow and never return, you never truly own.
- [The Marmot’s Well](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-marmots-well/): Be rude to the one who knows the way, and drink mud.
- [The Rich Man Who Became a Marmot](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-rich-man-who-became-a-marmot/): Give nothing to anyone, and you may lose it all.
- [The Wise Parrot](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-wise-parrot/): Heed the warning early; keep your head in the net.
- [The Wolf, the Fox and a Lump of Fat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-wolf-the-fox-and-a-lump-of-fat/): Cheat your partner, and you’ll be the one left ashamed.
- [The Three Companions and the Goose](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-three-companions-and-the-goose/): Scheme to cheat the hunter, and you’ll dream on an empty stomach.
- [The Orphan and the Wolf-King](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-orphan-and-the-wolf-king/): Spare the beggar, and listen when someone wise advises you.
- [The Owl Who Hid the Warm Land](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-owl-who-hid-the-warm-land/): Hide the warm place from others, and freeze alone.
- [The Girl Who Hid from the Moon](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-girl-who-hid-from-the-moon/): Keep your head, and even the Moon gives up the chase.
- [The Children in the Stranger’s Boat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-children-in-the-strangers-boat/): Never get into a stranger’s boat, whatever he says.
- [Raven and the Sea-Spirit’s Gifts](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/raven-and-the-sea-spirits-gifts/): Ask politely and thank the giver; mockery empties the house.
- [Wolves and Men](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/wolves-and-men/): Don’t drop a friend once you no longer need him.
- [The Wood-Master’s Sledge](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-wood-masters-sledge/): Mend what you break, and ask only for what you need.
- [The Old Man’s Clever Daughter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-old-mans-clever-daughter/): A quick answer can save someone you love.
- [The Girls in the Man-Eater’s Boat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-girls-in-the-man-eaters-boat/): Keep calm; a captor who turns his back gives you a boat.
- [The Boy Who Went Looking for His Father](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-boy-who-went-looking-for-his-father/): Keep asking until someone tells you the truth.
- [The Hare Who Kicked the Sun into the Sky](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-hare-who-kicked-the-sun-into-the-sky/): Even the smallest can bring back the light for everyone.
- [The Stingy Reindeer-Owners](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-stingy-reindeer-owners/): When you have food, share the best piece with your neighbour.
- [The Sea-Spirit and the Chief’s Daughter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-sea-spirit-and-the-chiefs-daughter/): A false hero’s boast sinks; the truth comes up in the net.
- [The Herd-Owner Who Turned to Stone](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-steppe-and-siberia/the-herd-owner-who-turned-to-stone/): Strike the hands that help you, and you’ll stand alone.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Tibet and the Himalaya (coming soon)

- [The Stone Lion](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-stone-lion/): Say “enough” before the bucket overflows.
- [The Pewter Vase](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-pewter-vase/): Cheat a friend with a trick, and a trick comes home.
- [The Bow by the Pool](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-bow-by-the-pool/): Try to keep it all, and you’ll end up with nothing.
- [The Pit-Digger’s Neighbour](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-pit-diggers-neighbour/): Dig a pit for your neighbour, and you’ll fall in it yourself.
- [The Man Who Shook Down the Monkeys](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-man-who-shook-down-the-monkeys/): Turn on the ones who saved you, and nobody saves you next.
- [The Jealous Fox](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-jealous-fox/): Whisper poison between friends, and it finds your own cup.
- [The Seven Dumplings](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-seven-dumplings/): Don’t judge a gift by its plain wrapping.
- [The Hundred Ounces of Silver](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-hundred-ounces-of-silver/): Claim more than you lost, and you lose it all.
- [The Turquoise on the Dragon’s Neck](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-turquoise-on-the-dragons-neck/): Be kind to Grandpa for himself, not for his treasure.
- [The Golden Duck](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-golden-duck/): Quarrel over who gets it all, and a stranger gets half.
- [The Cony in Bad Company](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-cony-in-bad-company/): Walk with thieves, and you’ll be judged a thief.
- [The Skin That Cooked Supper](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-skin-that-cooked-supper/): Spare the small ones; small hands find what you lose.
- [Dewa and the Ogress’s Children](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/dewa-and-the-ogresss-children/): Share with the hungry, even a monster, and the road opens.
- [The Tiger Who Wanted a House](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-tiger-who-wanted-a-house/): Three warnings ignored is three too many. Listen the first time.
- [The Kyang and the Rope](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-kyang-and-the-rope/): Tie yourself to a greedy plan, and it drags you.
- [The Frog Who Sharpened the Crow’s Beak](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-frog-who-sharpened-the-crows-beak/): Never take advice from your own dinner.
- [The Cat Who Took Up Prayer](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-cat-who-took-up-prayer/): When the cat turns holy, count your mice.
- [The King of the Mice](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-king-of-the-mice/): Lend to the little, and the little will save you.
- [The Toad Who Ate Tigers](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-toad-who-ate-tigers/): Panic runs fastest, and drags its friends behind it.
- [The Jackal Who Moved In](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-jackal-who-moved-in/): Bluff your way in, and the river finds you out.
- [The Monkey Who Called the Wind](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-monkey-who-called-the-wind/): Boast and you’ll fall; keep your head and you’ll climb out.
- [The Old Man in the Wedding Drum](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-old-man-in-the-wedding-drum/): Bring Grandpa along: strong arms need someone who knows how.
- [The Tiger and the Donkey](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-tiger-and-the-donkey/): Before you run from a guess, find out what really happened.
- [Sitoli and the Seventh Grain](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/sitoli-and-the-seventh-grain/): Hear “no”? Ask the next one, and the next. Someone will help.
- [The Hare Who Shared Out the Pack](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-hare-who-shared-out-the-pack/): Help a thief, and the thief will cheat you too.
- [The Four Friends](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-four-friends/): Honour the eldest, carry each other, and the forest thrives.
- [The Two Little Cats and the Handre](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-two-little-cats-and-the-handre/): Many small helpers can beat one big bully.
- [Sankhadhar Sakhwa and the Sand of Gold](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/sankhadhar-sakhwa-and-the-sand-of-gold/): Check the bottom of the basket before you shout “liar.”
- [The Headman’s Wise Wife](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-headmans-wise-wife/): Give the credit to the one who did the thinking.
- [The Donkey and the Rock on Trial](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-donkey-and-the-rock-on-trial/): Crowd round to laugh at trouble, and the joke’s on you.
- [The Lazy Son Who Found Things](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-lazy-son-who-found-things/): Keep your eyes open, even when you’re stuck in the pig-sty.
- [The Eastern Hero and the Western Hero](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-eastern-hero-and-the-western-hero/): However strong you grow, someone is stronger. Keep your boasts small.
- [The Monkeys Who Fished for the Moon](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-monkeys-who-fished-for-the-moon/): Follow a foolish leader, and you all fall in the well.
- [The Juggler’s Lesson](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-jugglers-lesson/): Don’t laugh at a skill you haven’t tried.
- [The Grey Old Woman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-grey-old-woman/): Share your bowl with the dog, and he’ll share his secrets.
- [The Violinist and the King Who Wanted Everything](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-violinist-and-the-king-who-wanted-everything/): Want everything you see, and you’ll walk through the wrong door.
- [When the Rivers Met](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/when-the-rivers-met/): Choose a guide who won’t stop to eat on the way.
- [The Fish King’s Gift](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-fish-kings-gift/): Try to take what’s someone else’s, and lose everything you had.
- [The Mouse Who Had a Tiger for a Son](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-mouse-who-had-a-tiger-for-a-son/): Pick on someone small, and meet the whole family.
- [The Bride Who Saved the Rice](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-tibet-and-the-himalaya/the-bride-who-saved-the-rice/): Save the grain others drop; one day it saves them.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Native North America (coming soon)

- [Why the Possum’s Tail Is Bare](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/why-the-possums-tail-is-bare/): Sing about your own beauty, and the whole world will laugh.
- [The Rabbit and the Tar Wolf](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/the-rabbit-and-the-tar-wolf/): Who won’t dig the well shouldn’t drink from it.
- [The Rabbit Goes Duck Hunting](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/the-rabbit-goes-duck-hunting/): Don’t claim you can do what you’ve only watched.
- [How the Squirrel Got His Blanket](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/how-the-squirrel-got-his-blanket/): Steal from someone’s store, and lose what you’re proudest of.
- [Two Lazy Hunters](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/two-lazy-hunters/): Lie about your work, and your shoes will tell on you.
- [How the Deer Got His Horns](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/how-the-deer-got-his-horns/): Cheat to win, and you won’t even get to run.
- [Rabbit and the Fire in the Grass](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/rabbit-and-the-fire-in-the-grass/): Brag that nothing scares you, and Trouble will come to look.
- [Why the Rabbit Steals](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/why-the-rabbit-steals/): Choose by looks alone, and you’ll go hungry.
- [How the Alligator’s Nose Was Broken](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/how-the-alligators-nose-was-broken/): Don’t crow about winning while the game is still being played.
- [The Owl and the Little Yellow Mouse](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/the-owl-and-the-little-yellow-mouse/): Fish for praise long enough, and you’ll catch the truth.
- [The Panther and the Crane](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/the-panther-and-the-crane/): Greed will eat you before you finish eating.
- [The Opossum’s Silver Tail](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/the-opossums-silver-tail/): Mock a neighbour, and you’ll run your own tail off.
- [The Raccoon and the Crabs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/the-raccoon-and-the-crabs/): Don’t dance at your enemy’s funeral until he’s buried.
- [The Turtle and the Beaver](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/the-turtle-and-the-beaver/): Take a home by force, and lose it to a quicker wit.
- [Wuchowsen, the Wind-Blower](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/wuchowsen-the-wind-blower/): Calm the storm, but leave the wind one wing.
- [Wihio and the Plums in the Water](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/wihio-and-the-plums-in-the-water/): Look up before you dive for what you want.
- [Where the Mice Danced](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/where-the-mice-danced/): Push in where you’re not invited, and you’ll wear it home.
- [The Turning Stones](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/the-turning-stones/): Use a gift as you were told, or it turns on you.
- [Wihio Becomes a Buffalo](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/wihio-becomes-a-buffalo/): Beg to be someone else, and you’ll forget how to be you.
- [How the Coyote Danced with the Blackbirds](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/how-the-coyote-danced-with-the-blackbirds/): Borrowed feathers fly only as long as the lenders like you.
- [The Coyote and the Locust](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/the-coyote-and-the-locust/): Mind your own business, and keep your teeth.
- [The Coyote and the Ravens Who Raced Their Eyes](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/the-coyote-and-the-ravens-who-raced-their-eyes/): Don’t hand over what you need for a trick you don’t understand.
- [How the Turtle Duped the Coyote](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/how-the-turtle-duped-the-coyote/): Bully someone out of his supper, and the supper bites back.
- [Iktomi and the Ducks](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/iktomi-and-the-ducks/): Trick the trusting, and the wolves eat your dinner.
- [Iktomi and the Muskrat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/iktomi-and-the-muskrat/): Share your pot, or you’ll beg for its bones.
- [Iktomi and the Coyote](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/iktomi-and-the-coyote/): Check that supper is really supper before you light the fire.
- [The Frogs and the Crane](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/the-frogs-and-the-crane/): Boast too loudly, and you tell the Crane where you are.
- [Iktomi and the Turtle](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/iktomi-and-the-turtle/): Flatter and cheat, and greed will pull you under.
- [Grizzly Bear and Beaver](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/grizzly-bear-and-beaver/): Show the weak no pity, and you will find none.
- [The Porcupine-Hunter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/the-porcupine-hunter/): Take more than you need, and the forest will remember.
- [The Discontented Grass Plant](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/the-discontented-grass-plant/): Be content as you are; envy leaves you on your own.
- [Txamsem and the Fishermen’s Bait](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/txamsem-and-the-fishermens-bait/): Steal the bait, and you’ll leave your jaw on the hook.
- [Beaver and Porcupine](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/beaver-and-porcupine/): A joke that strands a friend ends the friendship.
- [Coyote and His Guests](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/coyote-and-his-guests/): Never try what is beyond your power.
- [Coyote and the Humming-Birds](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/coyote-and-the-humming-birds/): What’s safe for a bird isn’t safe for you.
- [Coyote and the Fisherman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/coyote-and-the-fisherman/): Threaten to steal, and you may land on the hooks.
- [The Raven Who Wanted a Wife](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/the-raven-who-wanted-a-wife/): Don’t follow where you can’t land.
- [The Raven and the Goose](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/the-raven-and-the-goose/): Sneer at careful work, and you’ll get careless work instead.
- [When the Ravens Could Speak](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/when-the-ravens-could-speak/): Twist your words often enough, and you’ll lose them.
- [Qasiagssaq, the Great Liar](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-native-north-america/qasiagssaq-the-great-liar/): A liar runs out of fjord before he runs out of lies.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Mexico and Central America (coming soon)

- [The House That Said Good Afternoon](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-house-that-said-good-afternoon/): Whoever steals a small house won’t fit through its back door.
- [Uncle Coyote Keeps School](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/uncle-coyote-keeps-school/): If the job sounds too sweet, look inside the hive.
- [Uncle Coyote Holds Up the World](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/uncle-coyote-holds-up-the-world/): Let go of a lie, and the sky stays up.
- [The Third Prickly Pear](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-third-prickly-pear/): Greed swallows the spines with the fruit.
- [Coyote’s Fast](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/coyotes-fast/): A promise kept only when watched is not kept.
- [The Alligator Who Drank the Moon’s Milk](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-alligator-who-drank-the-moons-milk/): What you carry for the hungry is not yours to drink.
- [The Puma and the Bag of Chickens](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-puma-and-the-bag-of-chickens/): Threaten the one who saved you, and see what’s in the bag.
- [The Jaguar Cub and the Woodcutter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-jaguar-cub-and-the-woodcutter/): Pride that won’t listen learns from the wedge.
- [The Squirrel and the Gopher](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-squirrel-and-the-gopher/): Try to cheat your partner, and you’ll drag home an empty stalk.
- [The Eagle and Her Comadre the Hare](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-eagle-and-her-comadre-the-hare/): Ask, and ask again: one “yes” can set the whole world moving.
- [The Fox’s Honey Hole](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-foxs-honey-hole/): Before you reach in, ask who said it was honey.
- [Uncle Rabbit Rides the Alligator](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/uncle-rabbit-rides-the-alligator/): Never take a ride from someone who wants you for dinner.
- [The Dwarf of Uxmal](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-dwarf-of-uxmal/): Set a cruel test, and you may have to take it.
- [The Ants Who Made a Milpa](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-ants-who-made-a-milpa/): Seed hidden in a hollow tree feeds nobody.
- [What the Puma Told Her Cubs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/what-the-puma-told-her-cubs/): Climb the same tree twice, and the puma will be waiting.
- [The Rain God’s Servant](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-rain-gods-servant/): Don’t play with what you don’t know how to stop.
- [The Hunter Who Nursed the Wild Hogs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-hunter-who-nursed-the-wild-hogs/): Hurt it carelessly, and you’ll be the one who heals it.
- [The Deer-Hunter’s Bride](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-deer-hunters-bride/): Ignore the first warning, and there may not be a second.
- [The Hunter Who Ate the Snake](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-hunter-who-ate-the-snake/): When your friends all say don’t eat it, don’t.
- [The Hunter and the Talking Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-hunter-and-the-talking-tree/): Start home while it’s light; the dark comes faster than you think.
- [The Coyote Behind the Agave](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-coyote-behind-the-agave/): When you’re told not to swallow, don’t swallow.
- [The Blowfly’s Errand](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-blowflys-errand/): Tease what can’t fight back, and the whole forest hears.
- [The Boy and the Pot](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-boy-and-the-pot/): Leave the family its share, or the pot may keep your hand.
- [The Deer-Folk](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-deer-folk/): Don’t follow a stranger home, however sweet she seems.
- [Compadre Lightning and Compadre Serpent](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/compadre-lightning-and-compadre-serpent/): Spite that floods a town drowns the spiteful first.
- [The Old Man at the Door](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-old-man-at-the-door/): Before the door is barred, make sure everyone is home.
- [The King and the Boy Gathering Sticks](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-king-and-the-boy-gathering-sticks/): Do right even when someone swears that nobody will know.
- [Pedro de Urdemales Sells a Money Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/pedro-de-urdemales-sells-a-money-tree/): No tree grows money; only greed believes it does.
- [The Thief Who Was a Mule](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-thief-who-was-a-mule/): Kindness without sense buys the same mule twice.
- [The Lawyer’s Last Trick](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-lawyers-last-trick/): Teach a trick, and you’ll be the next one tricked.
- [The Apprentice Who Waited for Figs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-apprentice-who-waited-for-figs/): Wait for figs to fall in your mouth, and you’ll starve smiling.
- [The Mosquito Who Asked Who Was Bravest](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-mosquito-who-asked-who-was-bravest/): However strong you get, there’s always someone stronger.
- [The Duendes of La Loma](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-duendes-of-la-loma/): When someone says no, let go.
- [El Cotonudo](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/el-cotonudo/): Don’t laugh at a plain coat; you can’t see who’s inside.
- [The Proud Lady’s Somersault](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-proud-ladys-somersault/): Hold your nose at the sick, and you’ll land on your head.
- [Dead Man’s Alley](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/dead-mans-alley/): A promise made in trouble must be kept in good times.
- [El Cadejo](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/el-cadejo/): Do wrong in the dark, and the dark will give you away.
- [The Soldier Who Woke Up in Mexico](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-soldier-who-woke-up-in-mexico/): Tell the truth and stick to it; the ship will come in.
- [The Girl Who Drew a Train](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/the-girl-who-drew-a-train/): Don’t call someone wicked just because you can’t explain her.
- [Fihurití](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-mexico-and-central-america/fihurit/): You can’t move away from trouble you carry with you.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of South America (coming soon)

- [The Jaguar’s Bone Flute](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-jaguars-bone-flute/): Brag about your win, and the loser’s brother comes to listen.
- [The Tortoise Who Danced Away](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-tortoise-who-danced-away/): Don’t open the door because a sweet voice asks.
- [The Jaguar Sent to the Sun for Water](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-jaguar-sent-to-the-sun-for-water/): Help yourself to another’s meat, and you’ll come home to bones.
- [The Deer and the Jaguar Build a House](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-deer-and-the-jaguar-build-a-house/): Frighten the ones you live with, and nobody sleeps.
- [The Jaguar’s Travelling Companion](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-jaguars-travelling-companion/): A friend who sets traps for friends will step in one.
- [The Jaguar Who Wrestled Fire](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-jaguar-who-wrestled-fire/): Never try to swallow something that can burn you.
- [The Turtle Who Lent His Hooves](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-turtle-who-lent-his-hooves/): Never lend the feet you stand on.
- [The Woman Who Outwitted Two Jaguars](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-woman-who-outwitted-two-jaguars/): Get ready before dark, and let the night climb to you.
- [The Turtle Who Rolled Instead of Working](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-turtle-who-rolled-instead-of-working/): Fake the work, and you’ll live in the mess.
- [The Turtle and the Opossum’s Fast](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-turtle-and-the-opossums-fast/): Never bet your life on the other fellow’s strength.
- [The Candle-fly and the Lost Hunter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-candle-fly-and-the-lost-hunter/): Never laugh at help because it comes small.
- [The Birds Who Mocked Everyone](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-birds-who-mocked-everyone/): Mock everyone, and sooner or later you mock the wrong one.
- [The Evil-Eye Bird](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-evil-eye-bird/): Never point a thing you don’t understand.
- [The Curupira’s Roast](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-curupiras-roast/): Whatever you steal will speak up.
- [The Feast Nobody Cooked](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-feast-nobody-cooked/): Food you didn’t cook has a cook coming back.
- [The Man Who Claimed the Jaguar’s Kill](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-man-who-claimed-the-jaguars-kill/): Steal from the jaguar’s table, and you’ll be served at it.
- [The Gourd That Must Be Half Full](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-gourd-that-must-be-half-full/): Half full was the rule; greed filled it till it burst.
- [The Boys Who Ran from Work](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-boys-who-ran-from-work/): Angry at home? Stay and say so. Don’t run off alone.
- [The Girl Who Stayed Home](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-girl-who-stayed-home/): Go where your family goes; the forest visits whoever stays behind.
- [The Boy Who Said Her Name](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-boy-who-said-her-name/): When a kind stranger hides her back, look behind her.
- [The Wife Who Taught Her Husband to Hunt](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-wife-who-taught-her-husband-to-hunt/): Small bow, small birds, every day: that’s how hunters are made.
- [Ceiuci, the Hungry Old Woman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/ceiuci-the-hungry-old-woman/): Never laugh at hunger from a branch it can reach.
- [The Lucky Pot](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-lucky-pot/): Eat alone in secret, and soon you’ll eat nothing at all.
- [The Honey Wife](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-honey-wife/): A promise forgotten at a party is still a broken promise.
- [The Lazy Man and the Crab Baskets](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-lazy-man-and-the-crab-baskets/): Bring home seeds instead of crabs, and seeds are what you’ll eat.
- [The Hornets and the Gold](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-hornets-and-the-gold/): Throw hornets at your neighbour, and they may land as his gold.
- [The Man Who Wanted to Lasso God](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-man-who-wanted-to-lasso-god/): Cheat the friend who trusted you, and you’ll know no peace.
- [The Puma and the Fox](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-puma-and-the-fox/): The thief who brags is the thief who gets caught.
- [The Fox Who Went to the Feast in the Sky](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-fox-who-went-to-the-feast-in-the-sky/): Never insult the bird that is perched on your rope.
- [The Goose and the Sack of Birds](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-goose-and-the-sack-of-birds/): Let your anger go, or it will burst you.
- [The Grub Who Grew Proud](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-grub-who-grew-proud/): Lift your head too high, and the birds will notice.
- [The Tortoise and the Thorn Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-tortoise-and-the-thorn-tree/): A trick that’s safe for a shell isn’t safe for fur.
- [The Greedy Brother](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-greedy-brother/): Grab at a gift meant for someone else, and grow horns.
- [The Shepherd’s Last Song](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-shepherds-last-song/): In danger, call for help loudly; someone who loves you may hear.
- [The Fox and the Vulture](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-fox-and-the-vulture/): Never bet your skin against a bird with feathers.
- [The Fox and the Horsefly](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-fox-and-the-horsefly/): Lose the bet, then pay the bet.
- [The Honey-Gatherer Who Carried Fire](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-honey-gatherer-who-carried-fire/): Keep your head, and take a small bird’s good advice.
- [The Traro and the Vulture](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-traro-and-the-vulture/): Spend your strength at the start, and the sea takes the rest.
- [The Puma Who Played Dead](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-puma-who-played-dead/): Set a trap for others, and your own rope may take you.
- [The Free Colt and the Mule](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-south-america/the-free-colt-and-the-mule/): When the wild ones start running, don’t stand there talking.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of the Caribbean & African America (coming soon)

- [Anansi and the Queen Named Five](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/anansi-and-the-queen-named-five/): Set a trap with words, and your own mouth will spring it.
- [The Man-Crow](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/the-man-crow/): Steal the credit, and you’ll live in the rafters.
- [Ticky-Picky Boom-Boom](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/ticky-picky-boom-boom/): Repay a rescue with teeth, and you’ll eat alone.
- [Rat’s Wedding](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/rats-wedding/): Go back for the scrapings, and lose the whole feast.
- [The Cats’ Ball](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/the-cats-ball/): Hear something wrong? Say so, and get out before the lights go.
- [Anansi and Candlefly](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/anansi-and-candlefly/): Grab in the dark, and the light goes home without you.
- [Snake the Postman](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/snake-the-postman/): Pay with a friend’s head, and you’ll lose both friends.
- [Crab’s Corn-Piece](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/crabs-corn-piece/): Sleep on the watch, and someone else eats your pay.
- [Leap, Timber, Leap](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/leap-timber-leap/): Claim another’s work, and the next job will show whose it is.
- [Anansi in Crab Country](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/anansi-in-crab-country/): Climb into a sweet talker’s barrel, and you’ll come out red.
- [Gaulin’s Wedding](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/gaulins-wedding/): A borrowed suit falls off when the true tune plays.
- [Anansi and Tiger at the Blue Hole](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/anansi-and-tiger-at-the-blue-hole/): Teach a song your secret, and the song will tell it.
- [Anansi and the Roasted Plantains](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/anansi-and-the-roasted-plantains/): Send a friend on a fool’s errand, and someone is watching.
- [Anansi and the Cows](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/anansi-and-the-cows/): Lead a friend home on a rope, and the herd remembers.
- [Tumble-bug’s Butter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/tumble-bugs-butter/): Hit a friend over a fair share, and you’ll run forever.
- [The Horn-Tribe Party](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/the-horn-tribe-party/): Borrowed horns fall off at the first knock.
- [Fling-a-Mile](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/fling-a-mile/): Push a friend toward the hole, and your own hand slips in.
- [Brer Wolf and the Two Dinners](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/brer-wolf-and-the-two-dinners/): Wait to pick the bigger dinner, and you’ll eat neither.
- [Brer Squirrel’s Grace](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/brer-squirrels-grace/): Be sure of your dinner before you give thanks for it.
- [Brer Owl and Brer Rooster](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/brer-owl-and-brer-rooster/): Break your word to a friend, and the music stops.
- [Brer Rabbit’s Rock Soup](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/brer-rabbits-rock-soup/): A rock in the pot fools the hungry, not the cook.
- [Little Ox and Bouki](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/little-ox-and-bouki/): Someone asks where you sleep? Make sure your big friends know.
- [Brer Monkey Goes Looking for Trouble](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/brer-monkey-goes-looking-for-trouble/): Hunt trouble when it isn’t hunting you, and it bites.
- [Fowl-Hawk’s Boast](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/fowl-hawks-boast/): Brag you’ll never go hungry, and you’ll dive at a stump.
- [Inside the Cow](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/inside-the-cow/): Break the one rule you were given, and the door shuts.
- [Brer Partridge’s Share](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/brer-partridges-share/): The cheat who’s cheated has no one to complain to.
- [Brer Rabbit and the Ground-Mole](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/brer-rabbit-and-the-ground-mole/): Live on someone else’s work, and the work will tell.
- [The Broken Bargain](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/the-broken-bargain/): Skip your half of the work, and the bill comes due.
- [Brother Lion’s Pap](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/brother-lions-pap/): Ask advice from someone who won’t gain from your trouble.
- [Dry River](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/dry-river/): Asked three times to share? Share. A stubborn no costs everything.
- [Jogi Stays Awake](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/jogi-stays-awake/): In a stranger’s fine house, keep one eye open.
- [Watchman, Lion and Tiger](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/watchman-lion-and-tiger/): Tell someone at home where you’re going and when you’ll be back.
- [The Lard Girl](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/the-lard-girl/): Need help? Keep calling, louder, until a grown-up comes.
- [The Parrot Who Saw](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/the-parrot-who-saw/): Offered a gift to keep a bad secret? Fly off and tell.
- [Juan Bobo Sends the Pig to Mass](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/juan-bobo-sends-the-pig-to-mass/): Dress a pig in silk, and she still heads for the mud.
- [Juan Bobo Saves Himself Some Work](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/juan-bobo-saves-himself-some-work/): Every shortcut around work costs you the whole road.
- [Mr. Rainy-Day](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/mr-rainy-day/): Saving for a rainy day? Never hand it to a stranger.
- [The Girl Who Chose a Stranger](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/the-girl-who-chose-a-stranger/): Charming isn’t the same as kind; listen to those who love you.
- [Two Rocks and a Monkey’s Head](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/two-rocks-and-a-monkeys-head/): A bully gone quiet isn’t gone. Keep your guard up.
- [The Fiddler and the Dancing Beasts](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-the-caribbean-and-african-america/the-fiddler-and-the-dancing-beasts/): Keep playing; the beasts tire before the music does.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Polynesia (coming soon)

- [Rata’s Canoe](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/ratas-canoe/): Take without asking, and what you take will not stay yours.
- [Māui and the Fire of Mahuika](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/m-ui-and-the-fire-of-mahuika/): Play tricks with fire, and fire plays back.
- [Tiʻitiʻi and the Earthquake God](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/ti-iti-i-and-the-earthquake-god/): A bold heart wins fire; a bully keeps one arm.
- [Why the Weeds Grow Back](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/why-the-weeds-grow-back/): Look back at your work, and do it again forever.
- [The Brothers Who Cut the Fish](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/the-brothers-who-cut-the-fish/): Wait when you are told to wait, or live with crooked ground.
- [Kalokalo and the Sun’s Gift](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/kalokalo-and-the-suns-gift/): Open it before the wedding, and there won’t be a wedding.
- [Ina and the Smooth-Talking Thief](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/ina-and-the-smooth-talking-thief/): Beware the smooth talker who only wants to try it on.
- [Hina and Kuna of the Wailuku](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/hina-and-kuna-of-the-wailuku/): Dam the river to drown someone, and it boils for you.
- [Rata and the Boar Chase](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/rata-and-the-boar-chase/): Promised to keep out of it? Then keep out of it.
- [The Twins Who Went to the Sky](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/the-twins-who-went-to-the-sky/): Make home unbearable, and you’ll be watching it from far away.
- [Tāwhaki and the Rude In-Laws](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/t-whaki-and-the-rude-in-laws/): Load the stranger’s back, and you may be loading a chief’s.
- [Toa and Pale](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/toa-and-pale/): Stand tall when you should hide, and your brother pays for it.
- [The Sweet Potato That Rolled Home](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/the-sweet-potato-that-rolled-home/): Claim what isn’t yours, and it will roll right back home.
- [Punia and the King of Sharks](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/punia-and-the-king-of-sharks/): A king who believes every tale soon rules an empty sea.
- [The Rat and the Octopus](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/the-rat-and-the-octopus/): Bite the back that carries you, and the night sky hunts you.
- [Kahukura and the Fairy Net](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/kahukura-and-the-fairy-net/): Work in darkness, and the dawn will find you out.
- [The Swamphen and the Giant Clam](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/the-swamphen-and-the-giant-clam/): Take from everyone, and soon you’ll eat alone.
- [The Ant and the Rat](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/the-ant-and-the-rat/): Feast alone inside your fruit, and it becomes your house forever.
- [Fakapatu and the Giant of Tofua](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/fakapatu-and-the-giant-of-tofua/): Go looking for a fight, and it may disagree with you.
- [Kaehu and the Man-Eating Shark](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/kaehu-and-the-man-eating-shark/): The shark who waits for swimmers can be waited for.
- [The Bat Who Borrowed Wings](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/the-bat-who-borrowed-wings/): Lend what you can’t live without, and walk forever.
- [Tasi and the Owl](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/tasi-and-the-owl/): Pass by the one who calls for help, and you’ll come last.
- [Te Kanawa and the Fairies](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/te-kanawa-and-the-fairies/): Don’t go hunting on the fairies’ hill after dark.
- [Sina and the Eel](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/sina-and-the-eel/): What you feed too well may follow you everywhere.
- [The Ironwood Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/the-ironwood-tree/): Steal from a spirit’s tree, and the tree keeps you.
- [The Veka and the Kale](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/the-veka-and-the-kale/): Trap a neighbour for an insult, and wear the stripes.
- [Hanaʻaumoe the Flatterer](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/hana-aumoe-the-flatterer/): Sweet words on the beach mean teeth in the dark.
- [Kae and the Pet Whale](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/kae-and-the-pet-whale/): A stolen meal shows in your smile.
- [The Plover’s Daughter](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/the-plovers-daughter/): Mind how you treat the little bird; she may be the mother.
- [The Fisherman Who Gave Away Ten Fish](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/the-fisherman-who-gave-away-ten-fish/): Give your last fish, and you may keep your life.
- [Māui and Irawaru](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/m-ui-and-irawaru/): Refuse your share of the load, and walk on four legs.
- [Kaululāʻau, the Prince Who Pulled Up Trees](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/kaulul-au-the-prince-who-pulled-up-trees/): Pull up a people’s trees, and you’ll plant your own island.
- [Takarangi’s Water](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/takarangis-water/): Water given to an enemy can put out a war.
- [Taʻilaʻila, the Boy Without Arms or Legs](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/ta-ila-ila-the-boy-without-arms-or-legs/): Starve the one at home, and he eats what he guards.
- [Kihapiʻilani and the Bowl of Brine](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/kihapi-ilani-and-the-bowl-of-brine/): Throw brine at your brother, and taste salt for life.
- [The Thief Who Owned a Cave](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/the-thief-who-owned-a-cave/): A thief’s hiding place can close on the thief.
- [Hiro and King Puna’s Trees](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/hiro-and-king-punas-trees/): A gift from someone who wants something comes with a bill.
- [The Woman Who Pushed Up the Sky](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/the-woman-who-pushed-up-the-sky/): Pay after the work is done.
- [Pakaʻa’s Wind Gourd](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/paka-as-wind-gourd/): Throw away a faithful friend, and the wind remembers.
- [The Rattling Bones of Hua](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-polynesia/the-rattling-bones-of-hua/): Silence the truth-teller, and the sky stops speaking too.

## The Elder Millennial Chronicles: Tales of Melanesia, Micronesia and the Torres Strait (coming soon)

- [The Six Blind Brothers](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-six-blind-brothers/): Fish keep vanishing? Don’t blame your brother. Stay back and watch.
- [Bébi and the Two Wild Pigeons](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/b-bi-and-the-two-wild-pigeons/): When your sister says “not too far,” don’t go too far.
- [The Two Sisters and the Crab](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-two-sisters-and-the-crab/): Ate your sister’s crab? Own up. A fight can burn the house.
- [The Cheat Who Grabbed Both Iguanas](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-cheat-who-grabbed-both-iguanas/): Grab the whole catch, and one day the catch grabs back.
- [The Banana Trees That Cried](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-banana-trees-that-cried/): Don’t forget the things you planted. They still need you.
- [The Girl with Sores and the Kind Little Sister](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-girl-with-sores-and-the-kind-little-sister/): Be kind to the one the others push away.
- [The Man Without Firewood](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-man-without-firewood/): Fetch your firewood before the rain, not after.
- [The Turtle Who Wore the Bowl](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-turtle-who-wore-the-bowl/): What you steal, you carry on your back forever.
- [The Lizard Who Held His Breath](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-lizard-who-held-his-breath/): Cheat a friend twice, and the third time he’ll be watching.
- [The House of Mud](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-house-of-mud/): Sneer at a better roof, and the rain will show you why.
- [The Brush Turkeys](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-brush-turkeys/): Done something wrong? Go home and own up. Don’t run.
- [Kwahohofi and the Great Wave](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/kwahohofi-and-the-great-wave/): Someone keeps hurting people? Tell grown-ups. Together they can stop it.
- [The Greedy Cave Dwellers](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-greedy-cave-dwellers/): Shut the hungry out, and you’ll be the ones shut in.
- [Kapikoa’s Betel Husks](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/kapikoas-betel-husks/): Give your friends only the husks, and they won’t wait for you.
- [The Flute in the Corkwood Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-flute-in-the-corkwood-tree/): When the owner says “don’t climb up,” stay on the ground.
- [The Knot on the Waoi](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-knot-on-the-waoi/): Leave alone what’s marked as someone else’s.
- [The Ant in the House of Leaves](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-ant-in-the-house-of-leaves/): Hit out in a temper, and the fight comes back bigger.
- [The Man Who Picked Fruit Among the Dead](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-man-who-picked-fruit-among-the-dead/): Take nothing home from a place you were only allowed to visit.
- [The Wallaby on the Reef](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-wallaby-on-the-reef/): Mock everyone today, and nobody will carry you tomorrow.
- [The Cassowary Who Ate the Whole Tree](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-cassowary-who-ate-the-whole-tree/): Eat the whole tree, and you’ll end up on the ground.
- [The Fisherman and the Voice in the Dark](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-fisherman-and-the-voice-in-the-dark/): Something wrong about your friend? Get away and get help.
- [The Heron Who Paid His Debt](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-heron-who-paid-his-debt/): Help someone out of trouble, and one day they may help you.
- [The Rat and the Rail](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-rat-and-the-rail/): Share the fruit, not the stones, with the friend below.
- [The Pukeke and the Fowl](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-pukeke-and-the-fowl/): Do your friend’s turn as well as he did yours.
- [Tepete and the Ogress](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/tepete-and-the-ogress/): Stick together, and even the smallest can get you home.
- [Pwiopwio and the Fire-sticks](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/pwiopwio-and-the-fire-sticks/): Catch the thief before you blame the old man.
- [The Sea Behind the Fence](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-sea-behind-the-fence/): Hide a good thing from your neighbour, and you’ll both lose it.
- [The Sapless Bamboo](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-sapless-bamboo/): When your father offers, say yes; pride won’t fill your cup.
- [The Song for the Deaf Grandmother](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-song-for-the-deaf-grandmother/): Steal from someone who can’t hear, and someone else is watching.
- [One-Tooth Under the Rock](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/one-tooth-under-the-rock/): Never tell a stranger at the door where your mother went.
- [The Hawk Who Ate Everything](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-hawk-who-ate-everything/): Never tell a visitor your grown-ups are out. Tell your grown-ups.
- [The Mosquitoes of Oneata](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-mosquitoes-of-oneata/): Never swap something good for a basket you can’t see into.
- [The Four Chiefs Who Followed the Sun](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-four-chiefs-who-followed-the-sun/): Going far? Tell your family first. Homesick? Say so.
- [The Whale Who Wanted a Bow](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-whale-who-wanted-a-bow/): Bully someone small, and the small one may bring you down.
- [The Mouse Who Would Not Share](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-mouse-who-would-not-share/): Share your catch with the friend who shared your canoe.
- [Möqi and the Breadfruit Thief](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/m-qi-and-the-breadfruit-thief/): Climb a stranger’s tree for fruit, and she may catch you.
- [The Mosquito Stone](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-mosquito-stone/): Send harm to others, and it can blow back on you.
- [Asgordo and the Giant Donao](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/asgordo-and-the-giant-donao/): Don’t mock a poor home. Its owner may surprise you.
- [The Ogress Who Said She Was Granny](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-ogress-who-said-she-was-granny/): A stranger says she’s your granny? Stay outside and go home.
- [The Girl Who Chose Perfume](https://eldermillennialchronicles.com/tales-of-melanesia-micronesia-and-the-torres-strait/the-girl-who-chose-perfume/): Pretty won’t feed you. Choose what’s useful.
